# Jacob McCoy

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/jacob-mccoy/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Jacob McCoy

Conspirator

# Jacob McCoy

Filmmaker, and Director, Production at Third Wall Studio. We have made things together since Book of Sarth.

[Jacob McCoy](https://jacobmccoy.com/) is a filmmaker and visual artist working across documentary, music video and site-specific installation, and Director, Production at [Third Wall Studio](https://www.thirdwallstudio.com/). He directed, shot and edited the documentary on *The Gauntlet*, the choral and movement work by [Sxip Shirey](/conspirators/sxip-shirey/) and Coco Karol, streamed by the Sydney Opera House in 2020, and made the archival film for their *We Don’t Need the Sea to Drown* at National Sawdust in 2025 and 2026. He plays Linnstrument and bass.

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/VrtL59O1ps0)

> On March 2nd, 2015, Jacob and I got together to record some Linnstrument / Continuum Fingerboard duets. It was also Lou Reed's birthday, and this piece reminded me of things we explored together. Drones, close intervals, sum and difference frequencies. And Lou loved his Continuum Fingerboard. So this is dedicated to him.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [“For Lovers” on Vimeo, April 2015](https://vimeo.com/125323250)

## From Book of Sarth to Third Wall

He was one of the four people I thanked when [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/) was finished in 2012: Jacob McCoy is unstoppable. On March 2, 2015, Lou Reed’s birthday, we recorded Linnstrument and Continuum duets; one became “[For Lovers](/transmissions/singles/),” dedicated to Lou, filmed that spring and released as a single in 2020. He plays the Linnstrument drones on the second [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/) video, filmed and edited the two duets with [Sxip Shirey](/conspirators/sxip-shirey/) that same year, and plays bass on “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/).”

At [Third Wall Studio](/conspiracies/third-wall-studio/) he is Director, Production, and he directed three of the studio’s films, all made in [Burlap](/conspiracies/burlap/): *Meatsuitz – Dare to be Delicious*, a meat-themed swimwear ad, December 2025; *Meatsuitz Family Vacay*, January 2026; and *Through the Brambles*, the studio’s 360° VR film, May 2026.

The credit: Jacob McCoy and Sarth Calhoun: The Book of Sarth (2012), “For Lovers” (recorded March 2, 2015; single, 2020), Introspections (2015), “I Just Believe in Christmas” (2015, McCoy on bass), and Third Wall Studio, where McCoy is Director, Production and directed Meatsuitz – Dare to be Delicious (2025), Meatsuitz Family Vacay (2026) and Through the Brambles (2026).

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/ttWqwhzE-yA)

His films at Third Wall: “[Meatsuitz – Dare to be Delicious](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VrtL59O1ps0),” December 25, 2025. “[Meatsuitz Family Vacay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nZ2LpA9P-LY),” January 20, 2026. “[Through the Brambles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ttWqwhzE-yA),” 360° VR, May 11, 2026; drag to look around, or open it in YouTube VR. All directed by Jacob McCoy, made in Burlap at Third Wall Studio.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Doron Lev

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/doron-lev/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Doron Lev

Conspirator

# Doron Lev

Drummer, MC and illustrator. Drums on “I Just Believe in Christmas,” a guest on Beautiful Tornado, and three films at Third Wall Studio in 2026.

Doron Lev is a drummer, MC and illustrator, born in Miami to Israeli parents and based in Brooklyn, with a BFA in illustration from the School of Visual Arts. He leads the band Uglybraine, was music director for Rennie Harris’s *Funkedified* at the New Victory Theater in 2018 and for the Michael Jackson tribute *Invincible*, has toured with American Music Abroad, and has stage credits from *Break! The Urban Funk Spectacular* to Radio City’s *Spring Spectacular*. His visual work includes commissioned portraits, logos and community murals. He is an artist in residence at [Third Wall Studio](https://www.thirdwallstudio.com/).

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/fghXNj-HdBg)

> To finish the words I enlisted the help of some of my favorite creative people: Jesse Schoen, Virginia Piazza, and Doron Lev.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [on “I Just Believe in Christmas”](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/)

## Drums, a podcast, and three films

He is one of the three people I asked to help finish the words of “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/),” and he played the drums on it, at Figure 8 in August 2015. The first episode of [Beautiful Tornado](/transmissions/beautiful-tornado/), the podcast I made with [Dom Bouffard](/conspirators/dominic-bouffard/), is called “Waiting for Doron”; he is the guest on the second. “[Sometimes You Need Sun](/transmissions/singles/),” released in 2022 as Catfish Calhoun and Friends, is with him.

At [Third Wall Studio](/conspiracies/third-wall-studio/) three of his films came out in 2026, all made in [Burlap](/conspiracies/burlap/): *Truck Stop Love* and *Pigeon Problems* in February and *Watching Shadows* in April.

The credit: Doron Lev and Sarth Calhoun: “I Just Believe in Christmas” (2015, Lev on drums and words), Beautiful Tornado episodes 1 and 2 (2020), “Sometimes You Need Sun” (2022), and Third Wall Studio, where Lev is artist in residence: Truck Stop Love, Pigeon Problems and Watching Shadows (2026).

# Jonathan Arons

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/jonathan-arons/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Jonathan Arons

Conspirator

# Jonathan Arons

The dancing trombonist, artist in residence at Third Wall Studio. *The Trinary Matrix* is his film.

[Jonathan Arons](https://www.jonarons.com/) is a New York trombonist, dancer and entertainer known as the dancing trombonist, a member of the Chops Horns who has backed Alicia Keys, Aretha Franklin, Stevie Wonder and Mariah Carey and played in the *Dancing with the Stars* orchestra under Ray Chew; he played on the Dave Holland Big Band’s Grammy-winning *Overtime* (2005). He competed on *America’s Got Talent* in 2008 and 2025, holds degrees in jazz trombone and biochemistry from Oberlin, and wrote the memoir *Novelty Act* and *The Trinary Matrix*, a prequel to *The Matrix*. He tours with Gloria Gaynor.

[Embedded player](https://player.vimeo.com/video/1187032618?h=46e04bc8a5)

> Jonathan came in with a finished book. His own illustrations, his own story, all of it already on the page. What he needed was a way to bring it into motion without losing his hand in a pipeline. We set him up inside Burlap and showed him the canvas. He animated the book himself, scene by scene, the way a director works with a storyboard artist except he was both. We took it into post for editing, sound design, and finishing, and gave him back a film that still reads as his.
> 
> Third Wall Studio, [Process](https://www.thirdwallstudio.com/process)

## Third Wall Studio

He is an artist in residence at [Third Wall Studio](/conspiracies/third-wall-studio/), and *The Trinary Matrix*, from his book, is his film there: fourteen minutes fifteen, animated by him inside [Burlap](/conspiracies/burlap/) scene by scene, finished in post by the studio. The full film is above and on the [studio site](https://www.thirdwallstudio.com/).

The credit: Jonathan Arons is artist in residence at Third Wall Studio, founded by Sarth Calhoun; The Trinary Matrix (2026, 14:15), animated by Arons in Burlap and finished by the studio, is his film.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Tetiana Khodakivska

# Tetiana Khodakivska

Film director and editor, artist in residence at Third Wall Studio.

[Tetiana Khodakivska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetiana_Khodakivska) (born 1980, Kyiv) is a Ukrainian film director and editor based in New York since 2015, a member of the European Film Academy and the Ukrainian Film Academy. She won the Chicago International Film Festival Gold Plaque for the series *Angels of War* and the Golden Dzyga for editing *Foxter & Max*, and is a Sundance Institute grantee developing *The Blue Sweater with a Yellow Hole*, an animated documentary in which Ukrainian children returned from Russian “re-education” camps paint their memories.

## Third Wall Studio

She is an artist in residence at [Third Wall Studio](/conspiracies/third-wall-studio/), developing *The Blue Sweater with a Yellow Hole*, which spans four countries and three studios.

# Bora Yoon

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/bora-yoon/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Bora Yoon

Conspirator

# Bora Yoon

Composer, vocalist and sound artist. Her *Sunken Cathedral* was one of the first five gralbums, and she played the launch with me.

[Bora Yoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bora_Yoon_(American_musician)) (born 1980, Chicago) is a Korean-American composer, vocalist and sound artist, a TED2014 Fellow, who builds immersive soundscapes from voice, electronics, and found objects and instruments from many cultures and centuries. Her multimedia album *Sunken Cathedral* came out on Innova in 2014, with a release performance at Asia Society, New York, on April 23, 2014, featuring the kinetic sculptures of U-Ram Choe. She holds a PhD in composition from Princeton and teaches at Reed College.

![Bora Yoon performing at TED2014.](/images/conspirator-bora-yoon.jpg)

Bora Yoon performs at TED2014, March 2014. Photo: Borayoon, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:TED_Bora_Fellows.jpg).

> Additional thanks to The (Gr)album Collective artists Bora Yoon and Adam Matta for joining me in rocking the party on the downstairs stage.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [the launch announcement, April 9, 2014](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/)

## The Gralbum Collective

*Sunken Cathedral* was one of the five titles in the store when [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/) launched on April 9, 2014: her “O Pastor Animarum,” with a mechanical sculpture by U-Ram Choe and video by [Jacob McCoy](/conspirators/jacob-mccoy/) and Adam Larsen. She and [Adam Matta](/conspirators/adam-matta/) played the downstairs stage at the launch with me. Two weeks later my bio was in the program for her *Sunken Cathedral* performance at Asia Society, whose projection design was by Adam Larsen and Jacob McCoy of the collective.

The credit: The Gralbum Collective, founded by Sarth Calhoun, published Bora Yoon’s Sunken Cathedral gralbum in April 2014; Yoon played the launch, April 9, 2014, with Calhoun and Adam Matta.

# Billy Martin

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/billy-martin/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Billy Martin

Conspirator

# Billy Martin

Drummer of Medeski Martin & Wood, and a visual artist. His *Omnisphere* was a gralbum in the making.

[Billy Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Martin_(percussionist)) (born 1963, New York) is a drummer, percussionist, composer and visual artist, one third of Medeski Martin & Wood since 1991. He runs Amulet Records, played with John Lurie’s Lounge Lizards, and has published *Riddim: Clave of African Origin* and *Wandering*; his prints, paintings and drawings have been shown at the Cartagena Biennial and The Drawing Center. In 2026 he completed a Watermill Center residency with *The Start of Wind*, a theater work for a bamboo orchestra he built.

![Billy Martin, 2007.](/images/conspirator-billy-martin.jpg)

Billy Martin, July 2007. Photo: Hreinn Gudlaugsson, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Billy-Martin_DSC09238.jpg).

> The illustrations behind Billy Martin’s Omnisphere echoed of a Xenakis score. Bits of musical staff decorated with half-moons, C-clefs, and spiders floated in space.
> 
> Ariel Bitran, [Stereophile, April 23, 2014](https://www.stereophile.com/content/gralbum-re-thinking-concept-album)

## Omnisphere

[The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/) listed *Omnisphere*, his drawings with his music, as a coming title, and a preview was on the iPads at the launch on April 9, 2014. My old WordPress site had a conspirator page for him.

The credit: Billy Martin’s Omnisphere was a Gralbum Collective title in development, previewed at the collective’s launch on April 9, 2014; Sarth Calhoun founded the collective.

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Andrew Beck

Conspirator

# Andrew Beck

Lead programmer of the (gr)album app. We worked on it for three years.

> the duo worked together for three years and ended up creating a system that any artist could utilize to package his or her own album.
> 
> Ariel Bitran, [Stereophile, April 23, 2014](https://www.stereophile.com/content/gralbum-re-thinking-concept-album)

[Andrew Beck](https://www.linkedin.com/in/abeck99/) was the lead programmer of (gr)album, the iPad and iPhone app platform built to publish *The Book of Sarth* in October 2012 and, from April 2014, other artists’ gralbums. Stereophile, reporting from the launch, introduced him as “Lead Programmer Andrew Beck.” His later work is on his LinkedIn and [GitHub](https://github.com/abeck99).

## Book of Sarth and (gr)album

He built the app that became [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/), released in October 2012, and the platform behind [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/), launched on April 9, 2014, where the two of us were interviewed together. He is the first of the four people I thanked when the Book was finished: Andrew Beck was amazing.

The credit: Andrew Beck was lead programmer of The Book of Sarth (2012) and the (gr)album platform (2014), conceived and founded by Sarth Calhoun.

# Alex Wyly

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/alex-wyly/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Alex Wyly

Conspirator

# Alex Wyly

The artist of *The Book of Sarth*, credited as Alex Smith and thanked as Elik Smith. Now a designer of textiles and home furnishings.

> the art is beautiful unto itself, each page filled with inset images that shift, fade, or change.
> 
> Bryan Bishop, [The Verge, January 3, 2013](https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/3/3828314/the-book-of-sarth-ipad-app-graphic-novel-concept-album)

[Alexander Wyly](https://www.alexwyly.com) is the artist of *The Book of Sarth* (2012), credited on The Gralbum Collective’s title page as Alex Smith: “Art and Story: Alex Smith,” alongside illustrations by Tom Hall and [Archie P. Valdez](/conspirators/archie-p-valdez/). [Marc Urselli](/conspirators/marc-urselli/)’s review in Chain D.L.K. described the artwork as passing through several styles, from soft cartoon images to stylised vector work, treated black-and-white photographs and, by the epilogue, pixellated, almost art deco paintings. He now designs textiles and home furnishings, pillows, rugs, fabrics and wallcoverings, under his own name and as the brand [ALWY](https://www.wayfair.com/brand/bnd/alwy-b42123.html).

## Book of Sarth

He drew [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/), my first full-length solo release, two and a half years in the making. He is the second of the four people I thanked when it was finished, by the name I knew him by then: Elik Smith is a genius.

The credit: Alex Wyly (credited as Alex Smith, thanked as Elik Smith), art and story, and Sarth Calhoun, music, on The Book of Sarth, The Gralbum Collective, October 2012.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Adam Matta

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/adam-matta/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Adam Matta

Conspirator

# Adam Matta

Beatboxer, visual artist and animator. His *Sketches* was one of the first gralbums.

> It would be easy to wait for a plane and lose oneself in the moving paintings of Adam Matta.
> 
> Ariel Bitran, [Stereophile, April 23, 2014](https://www.stereophile.com/content/gralbum-re-thinking-concept-album)

Adam Matta is a human beatboxer and vocal performance artist from New York who has performed with Bobby McFerrin at Carnegie Hall and headlined the 2009 UK Human Beatbox Convention. He joined the [Carolina Chocolate Drops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Chocolate_Drops) in 2011 and plays beatbox and tambourine on their Grammy-nominated *Leaving Eden* (2012). His work has been featured on NPR and in the documentary *Planet B-Boy*; he also paints and makes stop-motion animation.

## Sketches

*Sketches* was one of the five titles at the launch of [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/) on April 9, 2014: one song, “Cellophane,” in which every sound is his unaltered voice, with 25 of his paintings and two stop-motion animations. He and [Bora Yoon](/conspirators/bora-yoon/) played the downstairs stage at the launch with me.

The credit: The Gralbum Collective, founded by Sarth Calhoun, published Adam Matta’s Sketches in April 2014; Matta played the launch, April 9, 2014, with Calhoun and Bora Yoon.

# Tom Hart

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/tom-hart/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Tom Hart

Conspirator

# Tom Hart

The artist of *Train O’ Thots*, drawn on the subway.

> We are excited to launch the Train O' Thots app on April 1st, 2015 with a special showing at the New York Transit Museum.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, sarth.net, March 28, 2015

Tom Hart is a New York artist who draws annotated portraits of subway riders during his commutes, by hand with fountain pen, brush and cut-paper collage, adding invented biographical text with “names changed to protect the peculiar.” Stereophile, at the Gralbum launch, saw NYC bums, metal-heads, and hipsters on the subway with gruff but comical drawings and incisive poetry.

## Two gralbums

[The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/) published *Train O’ Thots* in April 2014, his drawings and words with music by Moon Hooch, and *Train O’ Thoughts* in April 2015, with music by Exaltron ([Scott Hampton](/conspirators/scott-hampton/)) and me: “Hope is a state of Mind” is mine. The second launched with a showing at the New York Transit Museum on April 1, 2015. Video and animation on both were by [Jacob McCoy](/conspirators/jacob-mccoy/) and [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/).

The credit: The Gralbum Collective, founded by Sarth Calhoun, published Tom Hart’s Train O’ Thots (2014, music by Moon Hooch) and Train O’ Thoughts (2015, music by Exaltron and Calhoun).

# Joe Kelly

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/joe-kelly/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Joe Kelly

Conspirator

# Joe Kelly

Comics writer and filmmaker. The melody of my “Softly Questioning” became the main theme of his film *Poughkeepsie*.

[Joe Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kelly_(comics_writer)) (born 1971) is an American comic book writer known for *Deadpool*, *Uncanny X-Men*, *Action Comics*, *JLA*, *The Amazing Spider-Man* and the graphic novel *I Kill Giants*; as a co-founder of Man of Action he is one of the creators of *Ben 10*. He holds an MFA from NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts, where he teaches writing for animation and for comics.

*Poughkeepsie*, his second short film, was funded on Kickstarter in November and December 2015, shot in Nassau County, and premiered at the Long Island Film Festival on July 15, 2018. It is a 32-minute drama about George Dawes, a man with late-stage Alzheimer’s who finds he can go back into his memories.

![Joe Kelly speaking at WonderCon, 2012.](/images/conspirator-joe-kelly.jpg)

Joe Kelly at WonderCon, Anaheim, March 16, 2012. Photo: Gage Skidmore, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Kelly_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg).

The credit: Sarth Calhoun wrote the main melody of Joe Kelly’s short film Poughkeepsie (2018): the theme of “Softly Questioning,” from Reflections, Vol. 1, 2015.

## Poughkeepsie

The main melody of “Softly Questioning,” the third track of [*Reflections, Vol. 1*](/conspiracies/reflections-vol-1/), is the main melody of [*Poughkeepsie*](/conspiracies/poughkeepsie/). I recorded the piece in one take with [Lou Petto](/conspirators/lou-petto/) on drums and released it in November 2015, the month the film’s Kickstarter closed; the film was finished in 2018. I wrote about the connection when I revisited the record in November 2020, and I returned to the piece as “[Softly Questioning (Reprise)](/transmissions/singles/)” in May 2025.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Sxip Shirey

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/sxip-shirey/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Sxip Shirey

Conspirator

# Sxip Shirey

Composer, performer and storyteller. We recorded two improvised duets in 2015, his shruti box and prepared guitar against my Continuum.

Gene “[Sxip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sxip_Shirey)” Shirey is an American composer, performer and storyteller who grew up in Athens, Ohio, and moved to New York in the late 1980s. He works with found objects, rare and modified instruments, and electronics. He was a founding member of Luminescent Orchestrii, released the solo albums *Sombule* (2006) and *Sonic New York* (2010), and scored Neil Gaiman’s short film *Statuesque* (2009).

He was composer and music director of the circus production *LIMBO*, which toured from 2013 to 2019, and with the choreographer Coco Karol he created *The Gauntlet*, a site-specific choral and movement work first performed at National Sawdust in 2018 and since at the Sydney Opera House, Rockefeller Center and the Cleveland Museum of Art. He is a 2011 United States Artists Fellow and a curator and artist in residence at National Sawdust in Brooklyn.

![Sxip Shirey performing in 2010.](/images/conspirator-sxip-shirey.jpg)

Sxip Shirey performing, May 2010. Photo: Stacey~, [CC BY-SA 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sxip_Shirey_performing_in_2010.jpg).

> Sxip opens up a chord using levers on the Shruti Box, then uses his trusty SM 58 to mic highlight different notes within the chord, creating a melody within the drone.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [YouTube, May 29, 2015](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_ZinrLAl4I)

## Introspections

In 2015 he came to (Gr)album World Headquarters with an idea for a piece built on his shruti box, and in one day we recorded improvised duets at !N’Douglass Studios, filmed and edited by [Jacob McCoy](/conspirators/jacob-mccoy/) and mixed by Tim Knowlton. Two are on my YouTube channel: “Continuum Fingerboard vs. Shruti Box,” May 29, 2015, his amplified shruti box against the Continuum’s plucked-string model through a Sparkle Drive and a Marshall 4x10; and “Prepared Guitar and Continuum Fingerboard,” June 30, 2015, his guitar with paper clips on the strings and a harmonica to vibrate them, against a pulse code cello in Kyma. Both are part of [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/), and I have named him among the improvisers I explored those ideas with, alongside Laurie Anderson, Moldover, John Zorn, Marc Ribot and Rob Wasserman.

Jacob McCoy, who also plays the Linnstrument drones on the other Introspections duet, later directed, shot and edited the documentary on *The Gauntlet*.

The credit: Sxip Shirey, shruti box and prepared guitar, and Sarth Calhoun, Continuum Fingerboard: two improvised duets recorded at (Gr)album World Headquarters in 2015, part of Introspections.

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/V_ZinrLAl4I)

The two videos: “[Continuum Fingerboard vs. Shruti Box](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_ZinrLAl4I),” May 29, 2015, and “[Prepared Guitar and Continuum Fingerboard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8jgV_4Xqmc),” June 30, 2015. Sxip Shirey and Sarth Calhoun. Filmed and edited by Jacob McCoy; recorded and mixed by Tim Knowlton at !N’Douglass Studios.

## What I wrote under the videos

> Sxip Shirey visited (Gr)album World Headquarters last week with an idea for a really cool piece. This is based on his Shruti Box, which is a traditional Indian drone instrument working on bellows, similar to a harmonium ... or similar to an accordion.
> 
> Sxip opens up a chord using levers on the Shruti Box, then uses his trusty SM 58 to mic highlight different notes within the chord, creating a melody within the drone. The 58 is tun through an Electro-Harmonix Micro POG to add depth to the melody.
> 
> Sarth is playing the Haken Continuum Fingerboard, using an internal sound called Plucked String, a Karplus Strong physical model of a plectrum. The patch has an unusual property where it plucks more quickly the more you push. Moving forward and back on the continuum changes the length of the notes, allowing them to be distinct or blur together.
> 
> To have more control over the volume and timbre of the plectrum the continuum was routed through a Voodoo Lab Sparkle Drive and in to a Marshall 4x10 guitar amp.

> On the same day as our shruti/continuum duet, we played a few more pieces using different combinations of instruments.
> 
> This one was built around a pulse code cello sound in Kyma, controlled by the Continuum Fingerboard. Sxip thought the prepared guitar with reverb and pitch shifter would match the sound, and it really did!
> 
> The guitar has paper clips and such on the strings, and Sxip uses a harmonica to vibrate the strings.

My descriptions under the two videos on YouTube, May 29 and June 30, 2015, without the gear lists and credits.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Moldover

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/moldover/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Moldover

Conspirator

# Moldover

Musician and instrument designer, the coiner of controllerism. We shared Warper Party bills in New York and have improvised together.

Matthew [Moldover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldover) (born 1980), known as Moldover, is a musician, technologist and instrument designer based in San Francisco. He studied electronic music composition at Berklee, moved to New York to play in bands, and in 2005 coined the term controllerism for making music live with computer controllers and software; the MIDI Association has called him the Godfather of Controllerism. His instruments include the Mojo, the Robocaster, the Guitar Wing and a line of multiplayer Jamboxes, and he has performed at Sónar, Mutek and Coachella.

![Moldover performing at SHA2017, lit from below.](/images/conspirator-moldover.jpg)

Moldover performing “Step From Darkness,” SHA2017, the Netherlands, August 2017. Photo: Victor Bart, uploaded by Moldover, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Moldover_-_Step_From_Darkness_-_at_SHA2017_(by_Victor_Bart).jpg).

> I have been fortunate enough to explore these ideas with great improvisers, including Laurie Anderson, Moldover, John Zorn, Sxip Shirey, Marc Ribot and Rob Wasserman.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/)

## Warper Party and after

We were on the same bill at the Warper Party at The Delancey in New York on March 4, 2009, and Clocktower’s Warper Party Radio Extravaganza lists us both among its performers. On July 9, 2012 I posted about his Jamboxes on my old site, under [Contraptions](/contraptions/); only the title survives. I have named him among the improvisers I explored the [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/) ideas with, and my [CV](/work/) lists a video with him.

On December 30, 2025 his channel posted “Sarth plays Moldover’s Voice Crusher,” two and a half minutes of me on the Voice Crusher, the playable packaging of his album *Four Track*: a musical instrument that comes with the physical copy of the record.

The credit: Moldover and Sarth Calhoun shared Warper Party bills in New York in 2009; Calhoun names him among the improvisers behind Introspections, and lists a video with him.

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/DBrarrD8n_g)

The video: “[Sarth plays Moldover’s Voice Crusher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DBrarrD8n_g),” Moldover’s channel, December 30, 2025. The Voice Crusher is the playable packaging for [Four Track](https://moldover.bandcamp.com/album/four-track).

# Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/michael-patrick-flanagan-smith/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith

Conspirator

# Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith

Folksinger, playwright and writer. He sings “I Just Believe in Christmas.”

[Michael Patrick F. Smith](https://www.thegoodhand.org/) is a folksinger, playwright and writer from Frederick, Maryland. He ran Baltimore’s Living Room Company from 1999 to 2005 and moved to New York in 2011 to stage his play *Woody Guthrie Dreams* at Theater for the New City. As a musician he records and performs as The Good Hand. His first book, *The Good Hand: A Memoir of Work, Brotherhood, and Transformation in an American Boomtown* (Viking, 2021), recounts his time as an oil field hand in Williston, North Dakota; he testified to a U.S. House subcommittee in May 2021, and his reporting has appeared in The New York Times, The Washington Post Magazine and The Guardian. He lives in central Kentucky.

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/v-u7Zmd6GSw)

> Immediately I thought it should be sung by Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [on “I Just Believe in Christmas”](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/)

## The Christmas song and the podcast

The idea for “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/)” came out of a Christmas Eve 2014 email exchange with my Brooklyn neighbors, and I immediately thought it should be sung by him. We recorded it at Figure 8 in August 2015 and released it that December as Catfish Calhoun and Friends; his acoustic demo is on my YouTube channel. On February 15, 2021 he was the guest on the sixth episode of [Beautiful Tornado](/transmissions/beautiful-tornado/), “The Re-Enchantment of the World,” and played his covid-era songs live on the show.

The credit: Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith sings lead on Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas” (Catfish Calhoun and Friends, 2015) and was the guest on Beautiful Tornado, episode 6, February 15, 2021.

# Dominic Bouffard

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/dominic-bouffard/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Dominic Bouffard

Conspirator

# Dominic Bouffard

Guitarist and composer, a Robert Wilson regular. He played in the *Lulu* band in Berlin, on my Christmas song, and co-hosted Beautiful Tornado with me.

> This past August we all went in to the studio, along with a motley assortment of NYC instrumentalists ... plus my good friend Dominic Bouffard who was visiting from London .. and this was the result.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [on “I Just Believe in Christmas”](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/)

[Dom Bouffard](https://www.dombouffard.com/) is a London-born, Anglo-French guitarist, composer and multidisciplinary artist. He founded the rock band Sona Fariq in the early 2000s and now performs in the duo Emperors of Rome. With [Robert Wilson](/conspirators/robert-wilson/), who called him one of the most interesting musical talents we have today, he played guitar in *Lulu* (Berliner Ensemble, 2011) and *Shakespeare’s Sonnets* (2009), made the radio works *Monsters of Grace II* (2013) and *Tower of Babel* (2017, with Hal Willner), which won the Deutscher Hörspielpreis der ARD, and was composer, arranger and musical director for Wilson’s *Moby Dick* (Düsseldorf, 2024). He has worked with Lou Reed, Rufus and Martha Wainwright, Daniel Hope, Lady Gaga and CocoRosie.

## Berlin, Brooklyn, and a podcast

He played electric guitar in the Berliner Ensemble band for [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/), the production whose score Lou Reed and I wrote and whose music rehearsals I directed in Berlin in 2011. In August 2015 he was visiting from London and played guitars on “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/).” From March 2020 to February 2021 we made [Beautiful Tornado](/transmissions/beautiful-tornado/), six episodes of a podcast with guests including [Doron Lev](/conspirators/doron-lev/), Glen Brady, Richard Naviasky, Bryan Senti and [Michael Patrick F. Smith](/conspirators/michael-patrick-flanagan-smith/).

The credit: Dominic Bouffard and Sarth Calhoun: the Berliner Ensemble Lulu (2011; Bouffard on guitar in the band, Calhoun co-composer and rehearsal director), “I Just Believe in Christmas” (2015, guitars), and Beautiful Tornado (2020 to 2021, co-hosts).

# Marc Urselli

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/marc-urselli/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Marc Urselli

Conspirator

# Marc Urselli

Grammy-winning engineer. He reviewed *The Book of Sarth* and mixed my Christmas song.

> Marc Urselli did a thoughtful, in-depth review of The Book of Sarth over at Chain D.L.K. I appreciated the detail of his feedback, and even where it wasn't 100% positive I thought he made many great points. 4 out of 5 stars?! I'll take it.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [sarth.net, December 20, 2012](https://web.archive.org/web/20140909155440/http://www.sarth.net/chain-d-l-k-book-of-sarth-review/)

[Marc Urselli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Urselli) (born 1977, Aarau) is an Italian-Swiss audio engineer, producer and mixer based in New York, chief engineer at Eastside Sound and owner of Audio Confidential. He has won three Grammy Awards from seven nominations, with credits including U2, Foo Fighters, Lou Reed, Nick Cave, John Zorn and Laurie Anderson, and in 1994 he founded the online magazine Chain D.L.K., of which he is editor in chief.

## A review and a mix

He reviewed [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/) for [Chain D.L.K.](https://www.chaindlk.com/reviews/7353) on December 18, 2012, four stars out of five: three for the implementation, four for the content, five for the vision. Three years later he mixed “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/).”

The credit: Marc Urselli mixed Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas” (2015) and reviewed The Book of Sarth for Chain D.L.K. (December 18, 2012).

# Scott Hampton

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Scott Hampton

Conspirator

# Scott Hampton

Trumpeter, guitarist and composer who performs as Exaltron. He named *Reflections, Vol. 1* and plays its last track.

From the credits: Scott Hampton on Ukelele. Exaltron on Trumpet. *I Just Believe in Christmas*, Catfish Calhoun and Friends, 2015.

[Scott Hampton](https://www.scotthamptoncomposer.com/), who performs and releases as Exaltron, is a New York trumpeter, guitarist, music technologist and composer. He combines live instruments, looping and live remixing with custom Max for Live patches, has played The Knitting Factory, Nublu and The Delancey, toured nationally with [Moldover](/conspirators/moldover/), and in 2016 built a mobile sound system to take his looping rig into subway stations and parks. As a film and television composer he has scored features including *The Wayward Sun* (2013), *Batman & Jesus* (2017) and *Black Wake* (2018), and he teaches at Garnish Music Production School.

## A name, a track, and a gralbum

He gave [*Reflections, Vol. 1*](/conspiracies/reflections-vol-1/) its subtitle, *A Noise Akin to a Flight of Deranged Swallows in Combat*, lifted from a review of a [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) show, and Exaltron plays the last track: trumpet, guitar, guitar-bass and live looping. For [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/) he wrote two of the three songs of *Train O’ Thoughts* with [Tom Hart](/conspirators/tom-hart/), launched at the New York Transit Museum on April 1, 2015; the third, “Hope is a state of Mind,” is mine. He plays ukulele and, as Exaltron, trumpet on “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/).”

The credit: Scott Hampton (Exaltron) and Sarth Calhoun: Reflections, Vol. 1 (2015; Hampton named it and plays the last track), Train O’ Thoughts (The Gralbum Collective, 2015; music by Exaltron and Calhoun), and “I Just Believe in Christmas” (2015; ukulele and trumpet).

# Lou Reed

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/lou-reed/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Lou Reed

Conspirator

# Lou Reed

We met through Tai Chi and started with meditation music. Then came the song band, Metal Machine Trio, Yellow Pony and *Lulu*.

## Who Lou Reed was

Lou Reed (1942 to 2013) was an American songwriter, guitarist and singer. He co-founded the [Velvet Underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Velvet_Underground) in 1964 and wrote most of their songs, then made solo records for forty years, among them *Transformer*, *Berlin*, *Metal Machine Music*, *The Blue Mask*, *New York*, *Songs for Drella* with [John Cale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cale), and *Magic and Loss*. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the Velvet Underground in 1996 and as a solo artist in 2015. His last decade included *Hudson River Wind Meditations*, the Metal Machine Trio, the *Lulu* score for [Robert Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wilson_(director)), and the *Lulu* album with [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica).

![Metal Machine Trio on stage: Sarth Calhoun at his laptops, Lou Reed seated with guitar, Ulrich Krieger on saxophone.](/images/mm3-nyc-wide.jpg)

Metal Machine Trio in New York: Sarth Calhoun, Lou Reed, Ulrich Krieger.

> Lou decided to bring Sarth along at the last minute; he met him at tai chi practice, played with him at home and wanted his electronic sounds for this concert.
> 
> [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/), [“Unclassifiable”, The Wire, 2013](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/lou-reed-1942-2013_ulrich-krieger_unclassifiable)

## Before the noise

Lou and I met through Tai Chi, and we decided to do an album of meditation music together; it came out as the music of Master Ren Guangyi’s DVD, [*Power and Serenity*](/conspiracies/power-and-serenity/). That stuff was drones and melodies combined with pure noise, and we had talked about doing some duet shows performing it.

## Lou’s imagination

Lou invited me. Lou made all those decisions, but yeah, Lou invited me, and he wanted some fresh sounds. He wanted me to modernize the sound of what we were doing.

[Tony Diodore](/conspirators/tony-diodore/) once said that I was Lou’s imagination, when he wanted to just have some wild sound or some completely different kind of sound. That was what I brought.

> Reed performed an amazing set including ‘Dirty Blvd.’ and ‘Who Am I’ with Mike Rathke on guitar and Sarth Calhoun on electronic processing.
> 
> Lou Reed’s own site on the Whitney Museum show, [loureed.com, June 25, 2009](https://web.archive.org/web/20091014115819/http://www.loureed.com/00/archivexml.php)

![On a television stage: Kirk Hammett on guitar, Sarth Calhoun at his keyboard and laptop, Lars Ulrich at the drums, James Hetfield on guitar.](/images/lou-reed-metallica-2011.jpg)

With Metallica for *Lulu*, November 2011: Kirk Hammett, Sarth Calhoun, Lars Ulrich, James Hetfield.

## The projects

I did a tour with Lou’s [rock band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/) in the [spring of 2008](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), processing and sampling the instruments on stage. That fall Lou called me up about a free improvised noise gig at REDCAT in Los Angeles with [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/), and those nights became [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/). In 2009 I did two short tours with Lou and [Laurie Anderson](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/) as [Yellow Pony](/conspiracies/yellow-pony/). Then he called me to go over to his house and make some interstitial music for Robert Wilson’s *[Lulu](/conspiracies/lulu/)*, which turned into co-writing eight more songs, rehearsals in Berlin, and the record with Metallica. [“Junior Dad”](/conspiracies/junior-dad/) began at his apartment with [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/) and Kyma. I was still in the band for the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), and on stage with Lou and Metallica for the first live performances of the *Lulu* material that November.

## Iced Honey, with Metallica

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/6sf5euJJx6o)

The credit: Sarth Calhoun played Continuum Fingerboard and live electronics in Lou Reed’s touring band from 2008 through the 2011 European tour, was one third of Metal Machine Trio with Reed and Ulrich Krieger, toured Yellow Pony with Reed and Laurie Anderson in 2009, co-wrote the score for Robert Wilson’s *Lulu* with Reed, and played electronics on the Lou Reed and Metallica album.

My account is from an interview on August 25, 2026 and from the Metal Machine Trio, Lulu and Yellow Pony pages of my old WordPress site. Tai Chi and the meditation album are from the biography on that site. The video is *Later... with Jools Holland*, BBC, November 8, 2011.

# Laurie Anderson

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/laurie-anderson/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Laurie Anderson

Conspirator

# Laurie Anderson

[Laurie Anderson](https://laurieanderson.com/) is an American artist, composer and musician, born in Chicago in 1947. She trained in violin and sculpture, made performance work in New York through the 1970s, and reached number two on the UK singles chart in 1981 with [“O Superman”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O_Superman). She builds her own instruments, among them the tape-bow violin of 1977, which replaces the horsehair of the bow with recorded magnetic tape and puts a tape head in the bridge.

She met [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) in 1992 and was married to him from April 2008 until his death in 2013. I played with the two of them on the [Yellow Pony](/conspiracies/yellow-pony/) tours in 2009.

![Yellow Pony onstage, Madrid, 2009.](/images/yellow-pony-madrid-2009.jpg)

Yellow Pony, Madrid, July 2009.

## Yellow Pony

I first toured with Laurie as a trio along with Lou doing [“The Yellow Pony and Other Songs and Stories”](/conspiracies/yellow-pony/). It was a lovely two part tour that included outdoor performances in northern Spain, as well as my first visit to Copenhagen where I bought a really awesome plaid jacket that I wore until it was in tatters.

My role on that tour was to act as a bridge between the wildness of Lou and the grace of Laurie.

## What the room looked like

Dave Simpson reviewed the Manchester night for [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/jul/20/laurie-anderson-lou-reed-review) on July 20, 2009: The two titans faced each other – Anderson (standing) on violin and electronics, and Reed (seated) on various guitars – with electronic sound manipulator Sarth Calhoun between them. Over two hours, his expression transformed from enthusiastic glee to that of a baffled marriage counsellor, as Reed barked instructions.

The Paris house program at Salle Pleyel billed me as “claviers et électronique.” The full run is on [Sightings](/sightings/).

## Vivid LIVE

Anderson and Reed curated the 2010 edition of Vivid LIVE at the [Sydney Opera House](https://www.sydneyoperahouse.com/vivid-live/past-festival-lineups), running May 27 to June 11. Their program included Anderson’s own *Transitory Life*, a Noise Night, a tai chi event called *Power and Serenity*, and [Lou Reed’s Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/), which played the Opera Theatre on May 30, with me on Continuum and laptops.

## Afterwards

Since then every time I have joined her I think it was for a noise thing, in [Sydney](/conspiracies/vivid-live/), or at some of the drone shows. My favorite venue was the St. John the Divine show, I’ve always loved that cathedral, but my favorite show was probably the Winter Garden.

The credit: Sarth Calhoun played Continuum Fingerboard between Laurie Anderson and Lou Reed on the Yellow Pony tours of 2009, resampling their voices live, and has played with Anderson since: Vivid LIVE 2010, and the Lou Reed drone concerts at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, 2019, and the Winter Garden, 2023.

Both are on [Sightings](/sightings/): St. John the Divine on March 13, 2019, for what would have been Lou’s 77th birthday, and Brookfield Place Winter Garden on March 2, 2023, for his 81st.

---

# Ulrich Krieger

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Ulrich Krieger

Conspirator

# Ulrich Krieger

[Ulrich Krieger](http://www.ulrich-krieger.com/) is a German composer, saxophonist and improviser, born in [Freiburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freiburg_im_Breisgau) in 1962 and living in Los Angeles. He studied at the Manhattan School of Music and in Berlin, recorded the saxophone works of [John Cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cage) for Mode Records, and has been professor of composition and experimental sound practice at the [California Institute of the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Institute_of_the_Arts) since 2007. He calls his saxophone playing “acoustic electronics”: sounds that appear electronic but are made on an acoustic instrument.

He was one third of [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) with [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) and me, and he later played saxophone in [Reed’s song band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/) alongside me.

> Lou decided to bring Sarth along at the last minute; he met him at tai chi practice, played with him at home and wanted his electronic sounds for this concert.
> 
> [“Unclassifiable”, The Wire, November 2013](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/lou-reed-1942-2013_ulrich-krieger_unclassifiable)

## Metal Machine Music, scored

Krieger transcribed Reed’s *[Metal Machine Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Machine_Music)*, an hour of guitar feedback, for the Berlin ensemble zeitkratzer, scoring it for amplified acoustic instruments. The result was chamber instruments that sounded electronic. Zeitkratzer released the recording in 2007. That arrangement is how Reed came to know him.

## The genuine article

Ulrich is the genuine article.

I got to see a performance of his transcription of *Metal Machine Music* for orchestra, which is I believe what brought him to Lou’s attention, and it was stunning.

I always loved playing with him, the [MM3](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) shows could go from pure unrelenting noise to what [Laurie](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/) described as almost improvised classical music.

## Unclassifiable

Krieger wrote that essay for *The Wire* after Reed died in October 2013. It records two days of rehearsal at REDCAT, both shows sold out within twenty four hours, and late shows added.

He describes what the group became afterwards. At 2009’s Lollapalooza MM3 played a ten minute noise interlude between well known Reed songs to the frantic cheers of a large audience. On tour the trio set up four guitars and amplifiers as an opening sound installation, sometimes running for an hour before anyone walked on.

And what happened next. On subsequent tours with his newly revised rock group, including Sarth and me, he would play MM3 recordings before and after shows.

The credit: Ulrich Krieger and Sarth Calhoun were two thirds of Metal Machine Trio with Lou Reed, October 2008 to November 2010, and both played in Reed’s eight-piece band on the 2011 European tour. Krieger, tenor saxophone and live electronics; Calhoun, Continuum Fingerboard and live processing through Kyma.

## In Lou’s band

Krieger and I were both in the eight-piece band Reed took through Europe in July 2011, with [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/) on bass, [Kevin Hearn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hearn) on keys, [Aram Bajakian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aram_Bajakian) and [Tony Diodore](/conspirators/tony-diodore/) on guitars, and Tony Smith on drums. That run is on the page for the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), and the concerts are listed on [Sightings](/sightings/).

The Gramercy recording the trio made in April 2009 was later spatialised as an [ambisonic installation](/conspiracies/creation-of-the-universe-ambisonic/) that visitors walked into, standing where Reed, Krieger or I had stood.

My account is from September 23, 2026. “Almost improvised classical music” is Laurie Anderson’s phrase as I remember it.

---

# Rob Wasserman

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/rob-wasserman/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Rob Wasserman

Conspirator

# Rob Wasserman

Rob was always one of my heroes.

## Who Rob Wasserman was

Rob Wasserman (1952 to 2016) was an American bassist known for the electric upright bass that [Ned Steinberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Steinberger) built with him. His *Solo*, *Duets* and *Trios* records put the instrument in front rather than under everything else; *Duets* won a Grammy in 1989. He played for decades with [Bob Weir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Weir) as RatDog, and recorded with [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/), [Rickie Lee Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickie_Lee_Jones), [Van Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison), [Elvis Costello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Costello) and many others.

![Sarth Calhoun performing at Lollapalooza, a bass headstock in the foreground.](/images/lolla.jpg)

Sarth Calhoun at Lollapalooza, Chicago, August 2009. Rob Wasserman played bass in that band.

> Rob Wasserman’s upright electric bass, Kevin Hearn’s string/horn patches, Sarth Calhoun’s invisible Macbookery, and guitarist Steve Hunter’s fiery if decidedly inside-the-box solos.
> 
> Jesse Jarnow on the spring 2008 tour’s last night, [The Village Voice, May 6, 2008](https://villagevoice.com/2008/05/06/live-lou-reed-at-the-highline-ballrooms-first-birthday-party)

## “A huge fan”

What follows is the letter I wrote the day after Rob died, June 30, 2016.

I first met Rob Wasserman backstage at a performance of Lou Reed’s *Berlin* at St. Ann’s Warehouse. I walked up to him and shook his hand saying “Rob Wasserman! I’m a huge fan!”

My first instrument was the bass, and Rob was always one of my heroes. I became aware of him when his records, *Solo*, *Duo*, and *Trio*, redefined upright bass for me. I knew he was one of the people [Ned Steinberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Steinberger) worked with in creating those amazing electric uprights, which was Rob’s signature instrument.

He just chuckled and said “a huge fan ...” I couldn’t have imagined I would be on tour with him a few months later, backing up Lou Reed.

## The first sound

I remember so clearly the first time I played with Rob. Lou had invited me over to his apartment to show him what live processing would be like on stage. The source material turned out to be Rob bowing the electric upright, which I processed through [Kyma](/devices/). We recorded that first session, and it ended up being the basis for [“Junior Dad,”](/conspiracies/junior-dad/) the 19 minute outro to *[Lulu](/conspiracies/lulu/)*.

[Embedded player](https://open.spotify.com/embed/track/2zg2zQsXs0o6hCH9MTkZzw)

On record together: [*Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009*](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/), the official DVD, credits the band as Mike Rathke and Steve Hunter, guitars; Kevin Hearn, keyboards; Rob Wasserman, bass; Tony “Thunder” Smith, drums; Ulrich Krieger, saxophone; Sarth Calhoun, electronics and continuum. [loureed.com](https://loureed.com/news/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009-dvd/)

## The new guy

What I remember most dearly about Rob was how much he encouraged and supported me when I was the new guy in the band. He had as much or more reason than anyone on that stage to look on skeptically at this young whippersnapper, but instead he was unfailingly gracious. He always spoke to me with dignity and respect, as if I were an equal, which was status I had done nothing to earn.

I will never forget that generosity, and the world has lost another hero.

I wrote this the day after Rob died, June 30, 2016, and it is here as written. The backstage meeting was during *Berlin* at St. Ann’s Warehouse, December 14 to 17, 2006. Our first tour together was Lou Reed’s [spring 2008 U.S. tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/).

---

# Kevin Hearn

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/kevin-hearn/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Kevin Hearn

Conspirator

# Kevin Hearn

Keyboardist of Barenaked Ladies, and Lou Reed’s keyboardist and musical director from 2007 to 2013. We played in Lou’s band together from 2008.

[Kevin Hearn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hearn) (born 1969, Grimsby, Ontario) is a Canadian keyboardist, guitarist and composer based in Toronto, a member of Barenaked Ladies since 1995 and of Rheostatics, and leader of Kevin Hearn and Thin Buckle. He joined Lou Reed’s live band in 2007 and was Reed’s keyboardist and musical director until Reed’s death in 2013; their friendship began in 2001 with a phone call from Reed during Hearn’s treatment for leukemia. His solo records include *Mothball Mint*, *H-Wing* and *Days in Frames*, which carries “Floating,” a song about time spent with Reed in the hospital, recorded with Reed band members Fernando Saunders, Tony “Thunder” Smith, Mike Rathke and Aram Bajakian.

![Kevin Hearn, 2003.](/images/conspirator-kevin-hearn.jpg)

Kevin Hearn, July 2003. Photo: TheHYPO, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:KevinHearn3.jpg).

> Rob Wasserman’s upright electric bass, Kevin Hearn’s string/horn patches, Sarth Calhoun’s invisible Macbookery, and guitarist Steve Hunter’s fiery if decidedly inside-the-box solos.
> 
> Jesse Jarnow, [The Village Voice, May 6, 2008](https://www.villagevoice.com/live-lou-reed-at-the-highline-ballrooms-first-birthday-party/), on the Highline Ballroom show

## Lou Reed’s band

He was in the band around Lou at the first rehearsals at SIR in New York in April 2008: keyboards, mandolin, accordion and backing vocals on the [spring 2008 U.S. tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), keyboards at [Lollapalooza 2009](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/), and keys in the eight-piece band on the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/). On March 2, 2023, Lou Reed’s 81st birthday, we played a guest performance together at the Brookfield Place Winter Garden with [Shahzad Ismaily](/conspirators/shahzad-ismaily/) and [Laurie Anderson](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/), against Lou Reed’s Musical Drones performed by [Stewart Hurwood](/conspirators/stewart-hurwood/).

The credit: Kevin Hearn and Sarth Calhoun played together in Lou Reed’s band: the spring 2008 U.S. tour, Lollapalooza 2009 (on the DVD Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009), the 2011 European tour, and the Winter Garden guest performance for Reed’s 81st birthday, March 2, 2023.

![Lou Reed’s band on a club stage under red curtains, left to right: Rob Wasserman, Mike Rathke, Lou Reed, Sarth Calhoun, Tony “Thunder” Smith, John Zorn, Steve Hunter, Kevin Hearn.](/images/mwm-5113.jpg)

# Steve Hunter

# Steve Hunter

The guitarist of *Berlin* and *Rock ’n’ Roll Animal*. We played in Lou Reed’s band together in 2008 and 2009.

[Steve Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hunter) (born 1948, Decatur, Illinois) is an American guitarist, nicknamed “The Deacon” by the producer Bob Ezrin. He first played with Mitch Ryder’s band Detroit, whose cover of “Rock & Roll” led Lou Reed to recruit him; he played on *Berlin* (1973) and, with Dick Wagner, in the band on *Rock ’n’ Roll Animal* and *Lou Reed Live*, and wrote the intro to the live “Sweet Jane.” He has played on ten Alice Cooper albums beginning with *Billion Dollar Babies*, rejoined Reed for the staged *Berlin* in 2006 and its tours, and released *The Manhattan Blues Project* in 2013.

![Steve Hunter with a guitar, 2013.](/images/conspirator-steve-hunter.jpg)

> Jesse Jarnow, [The Village Voice, May 6, 2008](https://www.villagevoice.com/live-lou-reed-at-the-highline-ballrooms-first-birthday-party/), on the Highline Ballroom show

## Lou Reed’s band

He was in the band around Lou at the first rehearsals at SIR in April 2008 and on the [spring 2008 U.S. tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), guitars with [Mike Rathke](/conspirators/mike-rathke/) while I did electronics and live processing, and he plays guitar on [*Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009*](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/).

The credit: Steve Hunter and Sarth Calhoun played together in Lou Reed’s band on the spring 2008 U.S. tour, including the Highline Ballroom show of May 5, 2008, and at Lollapalooza 2009.

# Tony “Thunder” Smith

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/tony-thunder-smith/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Tony “Thunder” Smith

Conspirator

# Tony “Thunder” Smith

Lou Reed’s longest-serving drummer. We played in Lou’s band together from 2008 to 2011.

[Tony “Thunder” Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Thunder_Smith) is an American drummer, born in San Francisco, who played with Malo and on Santana’s *Welcome* (1973) before moving to New York for the Jan Hammer Group, and then spent four years as Serge Gainsbourg’s drummer. He held Lou Reed’s drum chair longer than any other drummer, recording *Set the Twilight Reeling* (1996), *Perfect Night: Live in London* (1998), *Ecstasy* (2000), *The Raven* (2003) and *Berlin: Live at St. Ann’s Warehouse* (2008). He is Professor of Percussion at Berklee College of Music.

![Tony “Thunder” Smith at the drums behind Lou Reed, on an outdoor stage.](/images/conspirator-tony-thunder-smith.jpg)

Tony “Thunder” Smith with Lou Reed, Hop Farm Festival, Kent, 2011. Photo: Man Alive!, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lou_Reed_and_Tony_Thunder_Smith.jpg).

The credit: Tony “Thunder” Smith and Sarth Calhoun played together in Lou Reed’s band: the spring 2008 U.S. tour, Lollapalooza 2009, and the 2011 European tour.

## Lou Reed’s band

He was the drummer in the band around Lou at the first rehearsals at SIR in April 2008 and on the [spring 2008 U.S. tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), at [Lollapalooza 2009](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/), and in the eight-piece band on the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), where I was on Continuum and Kyma.

# Aram Bajakian

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/aram-bajakian/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Aram Bajakian

Conspirator

# Aram Bajakian

Guitarist and composer. We played in the eight-piece band on Lou Reed’s 2011 European tour.

[Aram Bajakian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aram_Bajakian) (born 1977) is an American guitarist and composer of Armenian descent, based in Vancouver since 2013, who has toured with Lou Reed, John Zorn, Diana Krall and Madeleine Peyroux. [Marc Ribot](/conspirators/marc-ribot/) introduced him to Zorn, who released his first album, *Aram Bajakian’s Kef*, on Tzadik in 2011; later records include *Music Inspired by the Color of Pomegranates* (2015) and, with Dálava, *Understories* (2025). He teaches at Simon Fraser University and is a PhD candidate in ethnomusicology at the University of British Columbia.

![Aram Bajakian playing guitar at the Vancouver Jazz Festival, 2017.](/images/conspirator-aram-bajakian.jpg)

Aram Bajakian, Vancouver Jazz Festival, June 2017. Photo: Farhad Ghaderi, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aram_Bajakian_-_VancouverJazzFest-PhotoByFarhadGhaderi_9948.jpg).

The credit: Aram Bajakian, guitar, and Sarth Calhoun, Continuum and Kyma, in Lou Reed’s eight-piece band on the 2011 European tour.

## The 2011 European tour

By 2011 Lou was touring with eight people onstage, and he and [Tony Diodore](/conspirators/tony-diodore/) were the guitars, with me on Continuum and Kyma running multiple Pacas: the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), from Hop Farm on July 2 to Lyon on July 26. My road posts from that tour, the Hop Farm photos and the Carhaix clip, are the record of that band.

# Shahzad Ismaily

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/shahzad-ismaily/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Shahzad Ismaily

Conspirator

# Shahzad Ismaily

Multi-instrumentalist, producer and owner of Figure 8 Recording. We have played together in Lou Reed Drones.

[Shahzad Ismaily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahzad_Ismaily) (born 1972) is an American multi-instrumentalist, producer and studio owner based in New York, the son of Pakistani immigrants, who plays bass, guitar, banjo, drums, percussion and analog synthesizers and holds a master’s degree in biochemistry. He has been the bassist of Marc Ribot’s Ceramic Dog since 2006, scored the film *Frozen River* (2008), and has played on close to 400 records, among them Laurie Anderson’s *Homeland* and Arooj Aftab’s *Vulture Prince*; *Love in Exile*, with Aftab and Vijay Iyer, was nominated for a Grammy. He owns [Figure 8 Recording](https://www.figure8recording.com/) in Brooklyn.

![Shahzad Ismaily playing bass on stage, 2009.](/images/conspirator-shahzad-ismaily.jpg)

Shahzad Ismaily with Marc Ribot’s Ceramic Dog, Innsbruck, October 2009. Photo: Svíčková, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shahzad_Ismaily.JPG).

The credit: Shahzad Ismaily and Sarth Calhoun played together in Lou Reed Drones at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, March 13, 2019, and at the Brookfield Place Winter Garden, March 2, 2023; Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas” was recorded at Ismaily’s Figure 8 Recording in 2015.

## Lou Reed Drones

We were both participating musicians in Lou Reed Drones at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine on March 13, 2019, for Lou’s 77th birthday, curated by [Stewart Hurwood](/conspirators/stewart-hurwood/), with [Laurie Anderson](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/), [John Zorn](/conspirators/john-zorn/) and Stan Harrison. On March 2, 2023, Lou’s 81st birthday, the guest performance at the Brookfield Place Winter Garden was the two of us with [Kevin Hearn](/conspirators/kevin-hearn/) and Laurie Anderson. “[I Just Believe in Christmas](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/)” was recorded at his studio, Figure 8, in August 2015, by [Phil Weinrobe](/conspirators/phil-weinrobe/).

# John Zorn

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/john-zorn/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / John Zorn

Conspirator

# John Zorn

Composer and saxophonist. He played a set with Lou Reed’s band on my first tour, sat in with Metal Machine Trio, and shared the drones.

[John Zorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Zorn) (born 1953, New York) is an American composer, saxophonist, arranger and producer, a central figure of the downtown New York scene since the mid-1970s, whose work spans jazz, hardcore, classical, film music and Jewish music. He broke through with *The Big Gundown* (1986), led Naked City and Painkiller, and from 1994 to 2018 composed over three hundred Masada pieces. He founded Tzadik Records in 1995 and The Stone in 2005, was named a MacArthur Fellow in 2006, and was inducted into the Long Island Music Hall of Fame by Lou Reed in 2011.

![John Zorn with his saxophone at the Newport Jazz Festival, 2014.](/images/conspirator-john-zorn.jpg)

John Zorn at the Newport Jazz Festival, August 1, 2014. Photo: digboston, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:John_Zorn,_Newport_Jazz_Festival_2014.jpg).

> But it was the set-long appearance by saxophonist John Zorn that allowed all to hit their strides.
> 
> Jesse Jarnow, [The Village Voice, May 6, 2008](https://www.villagevoice.com/live-lou-reed-at-the-highline-ballrooms-first-birthday-party/), on the Highline Ballroom show

## Four nights

On May 5, 2008, the last night of my [first tour with Lou](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), he played most of the set with the band at the Highline Ballroom. On April 24, 2009, the second night of [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/)’s “A Night of Deep Noise” at the Blender Theater at Gramercy, he sat in; that night’s recording is the source of the ambisonic installation [*The Creation of the Universe*](/conspiracies/creation-of-the-universe-ambisonic/). In 2019 we both played Lou Reed Drones, at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine on March 13, where he opened on the organ, and at the Prospect Park Bandshell on August 3.

His Aleph-Bet Sound Project at the Contemporary Jewish Museum in San Francisco, 2008 to 2009, included Lou’s guitar processed through Kyma, which my site of the time linked as “The Conversation: Grace Memory.” I have named him among the improvisers I explored the [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/) ideas with.

The credit: John Zorn and Sarth Calhoun: the Highline Ballroom with Lou Reed’s band, May 5, 2008; Metal Machine Trio at the Blender Theater at Gramercy, April 24, 2009; Lou Reed Drones at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine, March 13, 2019, and the Prospect Park Bandshell, August 3, 2019.

![Lou Reed’s band on a club stage under red curtains, left to right: Rob Wasserman, Mike Rathke, Lou Reed, Sarth Calhoun, Tony “Thunder” Smith, John Zorn, Steve Hunter, Kevin Hearn.](/images/mwm-5113.jpg)

Lou Reed’s band at the Highline Ballroom, New York, May 5, 2008, the last night of the spring tour, with John Zorn. Photo: Mark McGauley.

Left to right: Rob Wasserman, Mike Rathke, Lou Reed, Sarth Calhoun, Tony “Thunder” Smith, John Zorn, Steve Hunter, Kevin Hearn. Highline Ballroom, May 5, 2008. Named by Sarth Calhoun, September 23, 2026. Photo: Mark McGauley.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Marc Ribot

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/marc-ribot/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Marc Ribot

Conspirator

# Marc Ribot

Guitarist. We played the ten-piece set at Noise Night, Sydney Opera House, 2010.

[Marc Ribot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Ribot) (born 1954, Newark) is an American guitarist and composer whose work spans no wave, free jazz, rock and Cuban music. A member of the Lounge Lizards in the late 1980s and Tom Waits’s guitarist since *Rain Dogs* (1985), he has played on records by Elvis Costello, Robert Plant and Alison Krauss, and Caetano Veloso, and is a long-standing John Zorn collaborator. He leads Ceramic Dog, with [Shahzad Ismaily](/conspirators/shahzad-ismaily/) and Ches Smith, and Los Cubanos Postizos; his albums include *Silent Movies* (2010), *Songs of Resistance 1942–2018* and *Map of a Blue City* (2025).

![Marc Ribot playing guitar on stage, 2007.](/images/conspirator-marc-ribot.jpg)

Marc Ribot live in Carmignano, July 2007. Photo: Andrea Mancini, [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Marc_Ribot_2007.jpg).

> I have been fortunate enough to explore these ideas with great improvisers, including Laurie Anderson, Moldover, John Zorn, Sxip Shirey, Marc Ribot and Rob Wasserman.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/)

## Noise Night, Sydney

At [Vivid LIVE](/conspiracies/vivid-live/), the festival Lou Reed and Laurie Anderson curated at the Sydney Opera House, the night after [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/)’s show was Noise Night, May 31, 2010: Zond, Melt-Banana, Bardo Pond with him as a guest, and a ten-piece collaboration led by Lou and Laurie with him on guitar and me on programming. My old site had a conspirator page for him with one post, “Photos of Noise Night, Sydney,” July 10, 2010; the post and its photos did not survive the site. I have named him among the improvisers I explored the [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/) ideas with.

The credit: Marc Ribot and Sarth Calhoun played in the ten-piece collaboration at Noise Night, Vivid LIVE, Sydney Opera House, May 31, 2010.

# Mike Rathke

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/mike-rathke/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Mike Rathke

Conspirator

# Mike Rathke

Lou Reed’s guitarist since *New York*. We played together in Lou’s band, as a trio at the Whitney, and on “Solsbury Hill.”

> Reed performed an amazing set including ‘Dirty Blvd.’ and ‘Who Am I’ with Mike Rathke on guitar and Sarth Calhoun on electronic processing.
> 
> [loureed.com, June 25, 2009](https://web.archive.org/web/20091014115819/http://www.loureed.com/00/archivexml.php), on the Whitney Museum opening

Mike Rathke is an American guitarist who was Lou Reed’s principal guitarist from the *New York* album (1989), on which he plays guitar and shares the mixing credit, and who co-wrote five songs on *Magic and Loss* (1992) with Reed; his credits run through *Perfect Night: Live in London* (1998) and *Animal Serenade* (2004). In a [PBS American Masters interview](https://www.pbs.org/wnet/americanmasters/archive/interview/mike-rathke/) he recalls meeting Reed the day after his guitars were stolen, when Reed handed him a guitar, and about ten years of writing music to Reed’s lyrics.

## Lou Reed’s band, a trio, and a record

He was one of the two guitarists, with [Steve Hunter](/conspirators/steve-hunter/), in the band around Lou when I joined for the [spring 2008 U.S. tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-spring-2008-tour/), and at [Lollapalooza 2009](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/). On June 23, 2009 the three of us played the opening of the Persol exhibition at the Whitney Museum of American Art as a trio: Lou, Mike on guitar, and me on electronic processing. We share a credit on Lou’s recording of Peter Gabriel’s “[Solsbury Hill](/transmissions/solsbury-hill/)”: additional guitar by him, additional programming by me.

The credit: Mike Rathke and Sarth Calhoun played together in Lou Reed’s band on the spring 2008 U.S. tour and at Lollapalooza 2009, as a trio with Reed at the Whitney Museum on June 23, 2009, and on Reed’s “Solsbury Hill” (Rathke, additional guitar; Calhoun, additional programming).

Left to right: Rob Wasserman, Mike Rathke, Lou Reed, Sarth Calhoun, Tony “Thunder” Smith, John Zorn, Steve Hunter, Kevin Hearn. Highline Ballroom, May 5, 2008. Named by Sarth Calhoun, September 23, 2026. Photo: Mark McGauley.

![Lou Reed’s band on a club stage under red curtains, left to right: Rob Wasserman, Mike Rathke, Lou Reed, Sarth Calhoun, Tony “Thunder” Smith, John Zorn, Steve Hunter, Kevin Hearn.](/images/mwm-5113.jpg)

Lou Reed’s band at the Highline Ballroom, New York, May 5, 2008, the last night of the spring tour, with John Zorn. Photo: Mark McGauley.

# Stewart Hurwood

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/stewart-hurwood/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Stewart Hurwood

Conspirator

# Stewart Hurwood

Lou Reed’s guitar tech, who performs Lou Reed Drones with Lou’s own guitars. I have played inside the drones since 2019.

The bill: 5:00 PM, Lou Reed’s Musical Drones performed by Stewart Hurwood. 8:00 PM, guest performances by Kevin Hearn, Sarth Calhoun, Shahzad Ismaily, Laurie Anderson. [Brookfield Place Winter Garden, March 2, 2023](https://web.archive.org/web/20230319094915/https://bfplny.com/lou-reed/).

[Stewart Hurwood](https://newyorklivearts.org/artists/stewart-hurwood/) is a guitar technician and sound engineer from near Cambridge, England, who moved to New York in 1995, toured with Duran Duran, and worked for Lou Reed as guitar tech and right-hand man for roughly the last ten years of Reed’s life. For the Metal Machine Trio tour Reed had him set four guitars and amplifiers feeding back as the foundation of the shows; after Reed’s death, at Laurie Anderson’s urging, he continued the work as Lou Reed Drones, performing with seven of Reed’s guitars and amplifiers at The Kitchen, the Prospect Park Bandshell, MASS MoCA, the Brighton Festival and the New Zealand Festival of the Arts.

## Metal Machine Trio and the drones

He was Lou’s tech through all my years in the band, 2008 to 2011; the photograph with Ulrich Krieger’s essay on Lou has the four of us at REDCAT in October 2008, the first [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) show. Since Lou died I have played in his drones three times: at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine on March 13, 2019, for Lou’s 77th birthday, which he curated, with [Laurie Anderson](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/), [John Zorn](/conspirators/john-zorn/), Stan Harrison and [Shahzad Ismaily](/conspirators/shahzad-ismaily/); at the Prospect Park Bandshell on August 3, 2019, International Lou Reed Tai Chi Day; and at the Brookfield Place Winter Garden on March 2, 2023, Lou’s 81st birthday, with [Kevin Hearn](/conspirators/kevin-hearn/), Shahzad Ismaily and Laurie Anderson.

The credit: Stewart Hurwood was Lou Reed’s guitar technician through Sarth Calhoun’s years with Reed (2008 to 2011); Calhoun has played in Hurwood’s Lou Reed Drones at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine (March 13, 2019), the Prospect Park Bandshell (August 3, 2019) and the Brookfield Place Winter Garden (March 2, 2023).

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Robert Wilson

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/robert-wilson/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Robert Wilson

Conspirator

# Robert Wilson

Theater director, 1941 to 2025. Lou Reed and I wrote the score for his *Lulu* at the Berliner Ensemble.

[Robert Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wilson_(director)) (1941, Waco, Texas, to 2025, Water Mill, New York) was an American director and playwright of experimental theater, also a designer, choreographer and visual artist, best known for *Einstein on the Beach* (1976, with Philip Glass) and *The Black Rider* (1990, with Tom Waits and William S. Burroughs). He founded The Watermill Center in 1991. With Lou Reed he made *Time Rocker* (1996) and *POEtry* (2000), and he directed Frank Wedekind’s [*Lulu*](https://robertwilson.com/lulu) at the Berliner Ensemble, premiered April 12, 2011, with music by Lou Reed; it toured to Paris, Spoleto and São Paulo.

![Robert Wilson, portrait, 2014.](/images/conspirator-robert-wilson.jpg)

Robert Wilson, Lübeck, January 2014. Photo: Cornel Wachter, [CC BY-SA 3.0 de](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:2014-01-19_Luebeck_Wachter_Wilson_(cropped_-_Robert_Wilson).jpg) (cropped).

> I got a call from Lou one day to go over to his house and make some "interstitial" music for a theater production. Robert Wilson was staging "Lulu" with the Berliner Ensemble. This turned into co-writing 8 more songs with Lou Reed.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [sarth.net, 2011](https://web.archive.org/web/20140905191203/http://www.sarth.net/category/conspiracies/lou-reed-metallica-project/)

## Lulu

Lou Reed and I wrote the music for his [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/). Lou did not travel to Berlin; I went, and directed the rehearsals of the music at the Berliner Ensemble in the spring of 2011. The touring program credits me among the music collaborators with Hal Willner and Ulrich Maiss. The songs became the album Lou made with [Metallica](/conspirators/metallica/) that autumn. Wilson and I were both among the people interviewed for Lou’s book on tai chi, *The Art of the Straight Line*.

The credit: Sarth Calhoun co-wrote, with Lou Reed, the score of Robert Wilson’s Lulu at the Berliner Ensemble (2011) and directed its music rehearsals in Berlin.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Metallica

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/metallica/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Metallica

Conspirator

# Metallica

The band. *Lulu*, 2011: our score, reinterpreted, and I played on every track.

[Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica) is the American heavy metal band formed in Los Angeles in 1981 by James Hetfield and Lars Ulrich; in 2011 the lineup was Hetfield, Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo. [*Lulu*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lulu_(Lou_Reed_and_Metallica_album)), its album with Lou Reed, was recorded from April to June 2011 at the band’s headquarters in San Rafael, California, and released on October 31, 2011. Its ten songs are based on the songs Reed wrote for Robert Wilson’s Berliner Ensemble production of *Lulu*. It was Reed’s last studio album.

![On a television stage: Kirk Hammett on guitar, Sarth Calhoun at his keyboard and laptop, Lars Ulrich at the drums, James Hetfield on guitar.](/images/lou-reed-metallica-2011.jpg)

Lou Reed and Metallica on television, November 2011: Kirk Hammett, Sarth Calhoun at his keyboard and laptop, Lars Ulrich, James Hetfield.

> A double-cd rendering of the entire collaboration between Lou Reed and Metallica, I was excited to have the opportunity to not only see our score reinterpreted by one of the greatest bands of all time, but also to play on every track.
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [sarth.net, November 6, 2011](https://web.archive.org/web/20140905192608/http://www.sarth.net/lulucd/)

## Lulu

After I got back from Berlin, we took the project to San Francisco and recorded it with them. They completely reinterpreted all the stuff. I play electronics on every track of [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/); “[Junior Dad](/conspiracies/junior-dad/)” began as a recording at Lou’s apartment. Then I played the first live performances of the material with them: *Later… with Jools Holland* in London on November 8, 2011, *Taratata* in Paris on November 9, and five songs at the WDR Funkhaus in Cologne on November 11.

The credit: Sarth Calhoun plays electronics on every track of Lulu by Lou Reed and Metallica (2011), which grew from the score he wrote with Reed for Robert Wilson’s Lulu, and performed it with the band on Later… with Jools Holland (November 8, 2011), Taratata (November 9) and at the WDR Funkhaus, Cologne (November 11).

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.
