# Leah Coloff

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/leah-coloff/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Leah Coloff

Conspirator

# Leah Coloff

[Leah Coloff](https://www.leahcoloff.com/) is a cellist, singer and songwriter in Brooklyn. She played cello and sang in [Number19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number19) from 1999, and she fronts [Lucibel Crater](/conspiracies/lucibel-crater/), the trio I started with her and drummer [Paul Chuffo](/conspirators/paul-chuffo/) in 2005. She also tours and records on her own, cello and voice with no other musicians, and she has played cello on other people’s records for years.

She and I have made three things together: Number19, Lucibel Crater, and [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/).

## Number19

Coloff, [Tony Diodore](/conspirators/tony-diodore/), Mark Righter and I formed Number19 in 1999. The band put looped cello and voice over bass and drums, and paid for its first record, *Suspension*, out of mp3.com downloads.

From the biography on my old site: Along his musical journeys, he met cellist and songwriter Leah Coloff, who convinced him to combine computers with music. The band they established, Number19, funded its first record with downloads from mp3.com in 2001.

## Lucibel Crater

I started Lucibel Crater in 2005 with Coloff on cello and voice and Paul Chuffo on drums. The trio released an EP, *Miracles*, in 2007 and a full-length, *The Family Album*, in 2008. [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) plays guitar on “Threadbare Funeral.” The live dates that survive in the record are on [Sightings](/sightings/).

## Book of Sarth

Coloff is one of the four people I named when [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/) was finished. Leah Coloff is a force of nature. She later released a gralbum of her own through the Gralbum Collective, the platform Book of Sarth was built to become.

The credit: Leah Coloff and Sarth Calhoun have played together since Number19 in 1999: Number19 (*Suspension*, 2001), Lucibel Crater (*Miracles*, 2007, and *The Family Album*, 2008), and *The Book of Sarth*, 2012.

## How I introduced her

> Leah Coloff is a Brooklyn-based cellist/singer/songwriter whose first album “Dark Sweet Heart” was greeted with critical praise and college radio play in the US. She tours and records as a solo act, cello and voice unaccompanied by other musicians or fancy machinery. She recently co-starred as Emily Dickinson in Ridge Theater’s “Lighting at Our Feet,” playing and singing music composed by [Michael Gordon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Gordon_(composer)). She’s contributed her cello to a long list of recording artists including [Ziggy Marley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziggy_Marley), [Rufus Wainwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Wainwright), [Dr. John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._John), [Nancy Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Sinatra), [Joel Thome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Thome), and [David Bowie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bowie). When performing with Lucibel Crater, Leah takes on many roles, one minute she’s a beat poet and her cello becomes an upright bass, the next she’s a cello playing hendrix, soul singing and feedback soloing.

I wrote that introduction for the conspirators section of my old WordPress site, recovered from the Wayback Machine.

# Paul Chuffo

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/paul-chuffo/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Paul Chuffo

Conspirator

# Paul Chuffo

Paul Chuffo is a drummer in New York. He was the original drummer for [Gutbucket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gutbucket_(band)), the punk and jazz band, and since 2005 he has played drums, thumb piano and sound in [Lucibel Crater](/conspiracies/lucibel-crater/) with [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/) and me.

## Lucibel Crater

Lucibel Crater has been a trio since I started it in 2005. A typical set begins with Chuffo’s syncopated drum parts being looped live, piece by piece, before the rest of the band builds on top of them. The trio released the EP *Miracles* in 2007 and the full-length *The Family Album* in 2008, with [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) playing guitar on “Threadbare Funeral.”

The dates that survive in the record run from the Knitting Factory in February 2007 through FatBaby, the Delancey and a Berlin night at RAW-Tempel in November 2008. They are listed on [Sightings](/sightings/).

The credit: Paul Chuffo has played drums in Lucibel Crater with Sarth Calhoun and Leah Coloff since 2005, on *Miracles*, 2007, and *The Family Album*, 2008.

## How I introduced him

> Paul Chuffo is a dynamic powerhouse who first caught the world’s attention as the original drummer for punk/jazz band Gutbucket, which [Modern Drummer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Drummer) described as, “a thrashing, squealing romp, full of shifting time signatures and punk-rock attitude.” He gives Lucibel Crater the joy and the energy to connect with your dancing feet.

I wrote that introduction for the conspirators section of my old WordPress site, recovered from the Wayback Machine.

# Mark Righter

In 2004 he founded Cambium Studio, a furniture design and build firm now in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, and he teaches part-time at Parsons School of Design.

# Tony Diodore

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/tony-diodore/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Tony Diodore

Conspirator

# Tony Diodore

Tony Diodore is a guitarist and violinist in Brooklyn. He has played in [Number19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Number19), [Puracane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puracane) and [BM LINX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BM_Linx). From 2011 he played guitar and violin in [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/)’s touring band, the same band I was already in.

## Number19

Diodore, [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/), Mark Righter and I formed Number19 in 1999, with Tony on guitar and violin. The band funded its first record, *Suspension*, out of mp3.com downloads, at one point sitting at number eighteen overall on the site.

## Puracane and BM LINX

After Number19, Diodore played guitar and violin on Puracane’s *I’ve Been Here the Longest* and co-wrote “Watershed.” In 2005 he formed BM LINX with Jonathan Murray. That band released *The Portable Genius* in 2006 and *Black Entertainment* in 2008, toured the United States, Canada and Europe, and went on hiatus in 2010.

## Back in the same band

A tour announcement on May 23, 2011 named Diodore as Lou Reed’s newly confirmed guitarist. He toured Europe that summer in [Lou’s band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/) on guitar and violin, and returned in 2012 for the *From VU to Lulu* European cycle, where Copenhagen, Bonn and Bordeaux coverage all name him. He also played the Wrecking Ball gala at St. Ann’s Warehouse with Lou on May 7, 2012. The dates are on [Sightings](/sightings/) and on the page for the [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/).

Tony once said that I was Lou’s imagination, when Lou wanted to just have some wild sound or some completely different kind of sound.

The credit: Tony Diodore and Sarth Calhoun formed Number19 together in 1999 (*Suspension*, 2001) and played together in Lou Reed’s band on the 2011 and 2012 European tours, Diodore on guitar and violin, Calhoun on Continuum and Kyma.

## How I introduced him

> Tony, Sarth, Leah Coloff, and Mark Righter formed Number19 in 1999. After we released Suspension, Tony went on to play with Puracane, and eventually form BM Linx. Now, Tony and Sarth have joined forces again, playing with Lou Reed.

I wrote that introduction for the conspirators section of my old WordPress site, recovered from the Wayback Machine.

# Rich Kulsar

Drummer and Grammy winner. We are both on Mike Acerbo’s *The Search*.

> You know who else is really featured on this record (besides Mike A) is Rich Kulsar and Leah Coloff … two great musicians who I get never enough chance to work with.

> Sarth Calhoun, [sarth.net, January 14, 2012](https://web.archive.org/web/20140905181543/http://www.sarth.net/category/conspiracies/mike-acerbo/)

[Rich Kulsar](https://www.monolisanyc.com/staff) is a drummer and percussionist working in New York since 1991, and co-owner of MonoLisa Studios in Long Island City. He won a Grammy in 2019 for Best Children’s Album as a member of Lucy Kalantari & the Jazz Cats, played drums on [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/)’s debut *Dark Sweet Heart* (1999) and on Mike Acerbo’s records, and his credits include Roger Waters, Micky Dolenz, Bruce Cockburn and Blood, Sweat & Tears.

## The Search

# Mike Acerbo

Conspirator

# Mike Acerbo

Singer-songwriter. I played bass on “Trilby,” the opening track of *The Search*.

> Mike did a wonderful job not only writing it but arranging it, singing it, playing guitar on it, and generally making it happen. As he should, since it is his thing. Go Mike!

[Mike Acerbo](https://mikeacerbo.bandcamp.com/) is a singer-songwriter born in the Bronx and raised in Pearl River, New York. His debut album *The Search*, recorded over about ten years from 2001, was released on February 14, 2012; its opening track is “Trilby.” A second album, *Dark Place*, recorded at Sear Sound and MonoLisa Studios with [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/) on cello and vocals and [Rich Kulsar](/conspirators/rich-kulsar/) on drums, followed in July 2026.

## Trilby

I played bass on “Trilby.” The first parts were recorded about a decade before the record came out, and I rediscovered my playing at the video release party in January 2012. On my old site the record was a conspiracy of its own.

The credit: Sarth Calhoun plays bass on “Trilby,” the opening track of Mike Acerbo’s The Search, 2012.

# Carla Scaletti

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/carla-scaletti/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Carla Scaletti

Conspirator

# Carla Scaletti

Composer and the inventor of Kyma. I beta-tested it, and my name is on the Kyma X startup screen.

[Carla Scaletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Scaletti) (born 1956, Ithaca, New York) is an American composer, harpist and music technologist, the inventor of the [Kyma](https://kyma.symbolicsound.com/) sound design language, first outlined in 1986, and co-founder with [Kurt Hebel](/conspirators/kurt-hebel/) of Symbolic Sound Corporation, spun out of the CERL Sound Group at the University of Illinois in 1989. She holds a DMA in composition from Illinois and received the SEAMUS Award in 2017; her works include *Trinity* (1989), *QUANTUM* (2013) and *misfold* (2023).

![Carla Scaletti, portrait, 2011.](/images/conspirator-carla-scaletti.jpg)

Carla Scaletti, April 2011. Photo: Kurt Hebel, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CarlaScaletti.jpg).

> I am glad to get this shout out from SSC because Kyma was so central to the sound and feel of The Book of Sarth, especially Primary Deforestation [vocal processing] and If I Can [pulse code cello played on continuum fingerboard].
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, [sarth.net, November 30, 2012](https://web.archive.org/web/20140906084650/http://www.sarth.net/symbolic-sound-book-of-sarth-review/)

## Kyma

I beta-tested [Kyma](/devices/) and am credited on the Kyma X startup screen. Kyma is under [Lucibel Crater](/conspiracies/lucibel-crater/), [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/), the [2011 Reed tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/), [Book of Sarth](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/) and “[Junior Dad](/conspiracies/junior-dad/),” and Symbolic Sound’s blog wrote about that work five times between April 2011 and November 2012, including a review of the Book. I have used Kyma to develop a kind of synthesis I call SeqOSC, a relative of AM synthesis derived from exploring the analogies between rhythm and timbre.

The credit: Sarth Calhoun beta-tested Kyma, made by Carla Scaletti and Kurt Hebel’s Symbolic Sound Corporation, and is credited on the Kyma X startup screen.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Kurt Hebel

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/kurt-hebel/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Kurt Hebel

Conspirator

# Kurt Hebel

Co-founder of Symbolic Sound and the designer of Kyma’s hardware: the Capybara, the Paca and the Pacarana.

> Here's Sarth preparing his rack-mounted Pacas for the tour.
> 
> [Symbolic Sound, the eighth nerve, July 26, 2011](https://news.symbolicsound.com/2011/07/lou-reeds-euro-tour/)

Kurt J. Hebel is co-founder and vice president of Symbolic Sound Corporation, founded in 1989 with [Carla Scaletti](/conspirators/carla-scaletti/), and the hardware and DSP designer behind Kyma’s sound engines: the Capybara and the later Paca and Pacarana. He holds a PhD in electrical and computer engineering from the University of Illinois, where he taught digital audio engineering before joining Symbolic Sound full-time in 1995; at the CERL Sound Group he built, with [Lippold Haken](/conspirators/lippold-haken/), the Platypus DSP in 1983.

## The orange boxes

The Paca, his dedicated DSP hardware for [Kyma](/devices/), is what I ran on stage: two on the [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) tour, rack-mounted Pacas on Lou Reed’s [2011 European tour](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/), and a Continuum with Kyma and a Paca in the Metallica sessions for [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/). I beta-tested Kyma and am credited on the Kyma X startup screen.

The credit: Kurt Hebel designed the Paca and Pacarana, the Kyma hardware Sarth Calhoun ran with Metal Machine Trio, on Lou Reed’s 2011 tour and on Lulu; Calhoun beta-tested Kyma.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Lippold Haken

https://www.sarth.net/conspirators/lippold-haken/

[Conspirators](/conspirators/) / Lippold Haken

Conspirator

# Lippold Haken

Inventor of the Continuum Fingerboard, my instrument.

> I lost sleep. I even dreamt about it last night. It was one of those thousands-of-people-watching nightmares.
> 
> Lippold Haken, after watching Sarth Calhoun play the Continuum at Lollapalooza, quoted on [sarth.net, 2010](https://web.archive.org/web/20101030053745/http://www.sarth.net/category/bio/)

[Lippold Haken](https://www.hakenaudio.com/the-team) (born 1961, Munich) is the inventor of the Continuum Fingerboard, a polyphonic touch surface that tracks each finger in three dimensions for continuous-pitch performance, and the founder of Haken Audio in Champaign, Illinois. He began the instrument in the early 1980s as a student in the CERL Sound Group at the University of Illinois, earned his PhD there in 1989, and taught electrical and computer engineering at Illinois until his retirement; Continuum sales began in 2000. With Edmund Eagan he developed the EaganMatrix, the synthesizer built into later Continuums.

## The Continuum

The [Continuum](/devices/) is my instrument: bass and melodies in [Lucibel Crater](/conspiracies/lucibel-crater/), Lou Reed’s band from 2008, [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/), where Lou and I both had Continuums on stage, [Yellow Pony](/conspiracies/yellow-pony/), the [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/) tapes and the Metallica sessions, and the duets of [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/). After watching videos of me playing it at [Lollapalooza](/transmissions/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009/), he said he lost sleep. The Continuum and Kyma come out of the same lab: he and [Kurt Hebel](/conspirators/kurt-hebel/) built the Platypus DSP together at CERL in 1983.

The credit: Lippold Haken invented the Continuum Fingerboard, Sarth Calhoun’s instrument since Lucibel Crater and in Lou Reed’s band, Metal Machine Trio, Yellow Pony and Lulu; Wikipedia’s Continuum article names Calhoun among its players.

The profile is from public sources, linked where they appear. What we made is the record on this site and the sources cited above.

# Transmissions

Filter writing

What went out: records, films, apps and writing. The collaborations that made them are [Conspiracies](/conspiracies/), and where they were played is [Sightings](/sightings/).

Records and songs.

  2020 to 2025. Eleven singles as Sarth on Noise | Groove, from “Squishy | Bass” to “Softly Questioning (Reprise),” and one as Catfish Calhoun and Friends.

  2020 to 2021. The podcast with Dom Bouffard: six conversations with musicians and artists.

  2012. A track from *The Book of Sarth*. Its melody is made out of a recording of 60 cycle hum.

  2011. The closing track of *Lulu*, nineteen and a half minutes. It began at Lou Reed’s apartment with Rob Wasserman’s bowed electric upright running through Kyma.

- ## [Peggy Sue](/transmissions/peggy-sue/)

  2010. Six pieces of tai chi meditation music composed and performed with Lou Reed for Master Ren Guangyi’s DVD, and only there: no CD was ever released. The first thing we worked on together.

  2008. Lucibel Crater, the trio of Leah Coloff, Paul Chuffo and me.

- ## [Miracles](/transmissions/miracles/)

  2007. Lucibel Crater’s EP, the year before *The Family Album*.

- ## [Suspension](/transmissions/suspension/)

  2001. Number19, the band I formed in 1999 with Tony Diodore, Leah Coloff and Mark Righter.

## Lexical

Essays and writing.

- ## [DuckDB, where have you been all my life](/transmissions/duckdb-where-have-you-been-all-my-life/)

  Sep 22, 2026. Asking Claude how much an artist spent on a project in Burlap, answered straight from JSON files with DuckDB. Plus the whole append-only pipeline pattern, on a laptop.

- ## [External Tables, Partitions, CTEs, Window Functions, and Partitions](/transmissions/external-tables/)

  Tutorial series, five parts. Building an append-only data pipeline on external tables, with window functions for the current truth and runtime type checking at the boundary.

- ## [Window functions, the mental model](/transmissions/window-functions/)

  SQL. Compare them to aggregates, PARTITION BY vs GROUP BY, ROW_NUMBER vs RANK, and why the window grows.

- ## [SQL as the data language](/transmissions/sql-as-the-data-language/)

  SQL. Views, CTEs, joins, and why everything is a table (which is also not true).

- ## [You might not need Pandas](/transmissions/you-might-not-need-pandas/)

  Essay. Most day to day Pandas work is better done in SQL, with a side by side example, and where Pandas still earns its place.

- ## [Why Python is the default for data work](/transmissions/why-python-is-the-default-for-data-work/)

  Essay. It is what people know, plus an ecosystem written in C, C++ and CUDA. What that does and does not tell you about building pipelines.

- ## [Modern Postgres is shockingly capable](/transmissions/modern-postgres/)

  Essay. JSONB, horizontal scaling, and the rise and fall of MongoDB.

- ## [Node vs Rails: agnostic vs batteries included](/transmissions/node-vs-rails/)

  Essay. The case that an agnostic server beats batteries included, and why I am not sure I believe it.

- ## [Visual Reference Prompting](/transmissions/visual-reference-prompting/)

  Jul 31, 2026. How original images can hold a subject together, bend a style, and open up stranger places to go next.

- ## [About Awakening (To Blacklist)](/transmissions/about-awakening-to-blacklist/)

  Nov 21, 2020. How the track’s melody came out of a recording of 60 cycle hum: a frequency shifter on the Spacebirds preset, wet/dry automation, and a happy accident with two frozen drum tracks. With the audio examples.

## For Lovers

October 30, 2020. 8:32. With Jacob McCoy. The 2015 Linnstrument and Continuum duet from [Introspections](/transmissions/introspections/), released as a single five years later. On [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/album/1eYowG2sDJhykbBMc1nk3g) and [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/1537204819).

On March 2nd, 2015, Jacob and I got together to record some Linnstrument / Continuum Fingerboard duets. It was also Lou Reed’s birthday, and this piece reminded me of things we explored together. Drones, close intervals, sum and difference frequencies. And Lou loved his Continuum Fingerboard. So this is dedicated to him.

# Beautiful Tornado

*Beautiful Tornado* is the podcast Dom Bouffard and I made: six long conversations with musicians and artists, recorded in 2020 and 2021. It is on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLmXj9m6I5JooEjI2skmu1LdMlhlmYaTfb) and [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/beautiful-tornado/id1553841403).

![Beautiful Tornado podcast cover: an abstract drawing in red, black and blue.](/images/beautiful-tornado-cover.jpg)

Cover, *Beautiful Tornado*.

> It’s like a dirty secret. A place where musicians and artists talk about the kind of stuff they love to talk about, but their girlfriends / boyfriends don’t. We’ll be chatting to amazing and original creators around the world about new releases, how they think about what they do, whether robots will kill us all and if peyote is as good on cornflakes as on Rice Crispies... that kinda thing..
> 
> The show’s own description

## The episodes

- **1. Waiting for Doron.** Dom and Sarth grapple with technical issues, talk about latest releases, and wonder when Doron might show up. March 30, 2020. 34 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rBXxj085FSk)

- **2. More Egg than Egg.** With Doron Lev. 1 h 34 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qgnKGljOBRE)

- **3. I Was Ready.** With Glen Brady, DJ, producer and former Irish DMC scratch champion, aka The Glass, DJ Wool and Blackwater Hardware, on his career from New York, Berlin and California to musician and survivalist in the Irish countryside. 1 h 25 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MkGrvP7A1dA)

- **4. Richard Naviasky’s Positivity Mission.** Songwriter, poet, firefighter, transatlantic sailor, dad. Rich Nav on round bottoms, why music’s better than art, and crapping off the side of boats. November 17, 2020. 42 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GxIDY9XvvaA)

- **5. Bryan Senti.** A musician, composer and producer from New York, now working in Hollywood. Platonic ideals, metric modulation, beta blockers and the joy of performance. 1 h 45 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SkvCEhxo4-g)

- **6. The Re-Enchantment of the World.** With Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith, singer-songwriter, playwright and novelist, from New York to Kentucky via a North Dakota oil town, with covid-era songs performed live. February 15, 2021. 2 h 26 min.

  [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDAzJr382Ho)

## Conspiracies

Dom Bouffard played guitar in the Berliner Ensemble band for [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/) and on [“I Just Believe in Christmas”](/conspiracies/i-just-believe-in-christmas/). Doron Lev, of episode two, drums on that song and makes films at [Third Wall Studio](/conspiracies/third-wall-studio/). Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith, of episode six, sings it.

The credit: *Beautiful Tornado* was made by Sarth Calhoun and Dom Bouffard: six episodes, March 2020 to February 2021.

The YouTube banner.

Episode list and lengths from the YouTube playlist; dates from the podcast feeds where they carry them. The description is the show’s own.

# Transmissions from the Book of Sarth

https://www.sarth.net/transmissions/transmissions-from-the-book-of-sarth/

[Transmissions](/transmissions/) / Transmissions from the Book of Sarth

Transmission · Dream

# *Transmissions from the Book of Sarth*

*Transmissions from the Book of Sarth* is a four-track EP I released in 2013 from the music of [*The Book of Sarth*](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/), the graphic novel and concept album I built as an iPad app the year before. The score was made with [Kyma](/devices/).

![Cover of Transmissions from the Book of Sarth.](/images/art-transmissions-from-the-book-of-sarth.jpg)

Cover, *Transmissions from the Book of Sarth*, 2013.

[Embedded player](https://open.spotify.com/embed/album/2AK3ADNcGHccdecSkjV43k)

## Listen

Four pieces: “Awakening (To Blacklist),” “Table (If I Can),” “Primary Defenestration (Deforestation)” and “For Valentina (To Your Rescue).” The first has [its own page](/conspiracies/awakening-to-blacklist/): its melody is made out of a recording of 60 cycle hum. On [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/album/2AK3ADNcGHccdecSkjV43k).

## The hum

One of my favorite things about this track is the morph from the hum to a rhythmic/pitched pattern. There’s a scene in ‘Book of Sarth’ where the office workers are coming out of a daze, they are transitioning back in to reality, and the hum transforming really ended up matching this perfectly. (I don’t know which idea came first.)

I start with a recording of typical 60 cycle hum. This was pretty straightforward, I probably just messed with a 1/4” cable partially plugged into my Marshall amp, or something similar. I wanted to see if I could transform that sound into something.

The whole of that, with the audio examples, is on its own page: [About Awakening (To Blacklist)](/transmissions/about-awakening-to-blacklist/).

![Artwork from The Book of Sarth: koi in three panels.](/images/book-of-sarth-fish.jpg)

From *The Book of Sarth*.

> Calhoun’s music is no doubt experimental, but his tracks and the artwork play nimbly off one another.
> 
> Bryan Bishop, [The Verge, January 3, 2013](https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/3/3828314/the-book-of-sarth-ipad-app-graphic-novel-concept-album)

## Conspiracies

The music of [*The Book of Sarth*](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/), released as a record a year after the app. Published through [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/). The app is at [bookofsarth.com](https://bookofsarth.com).

The credit: *Transmissions from the Book of Sarth*, 2013: four pieces by Sarth Calhoun from the music of *The Book of Sarth*, made with Kyma, published through The Gralbum Collective.

My paragraphs on the hum are from “About Awakening (To Blacklist)” on my site, November 21, 2020. Track list from Spotify.

# Solsbury Hill

https://www.sarth.net/transmissions/solsbury-hill/

[Transmissions](/transmissions/) / Solsbury Hill

Transmission · Dream

# “Solsbury Hill”

“Solsbury Hill” is [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/)’s recording of the Peter Gabriel song for *And I’ll Scratch Yours*, the companion to Gabriel’s *Scratch My Back*, released on Real World Records in September 2013. Gabriel had covered Reed’s “The Power of the Heart” on his side of the exchange; Reed returned Gabriel’s 1977 song. I produced it and played electronics on it. Track eleven, five minutes twenty-four.

![Cover of Peter Gabriel: And I'll Scratch Yours.](/images/art-and-ill-scratch-yours.jpg)

Cover, *And I’ll Scratch Yours*, 2013.

The credit: Production and electronics, Sarth Calhoun. Discogs, [release 4938695](https://www.discogs.com/release/4938695), track 11, lists additional programming. On [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/987512394) and [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/track/1PO2HeYYaAm5GDoqQsuRQz).

## Listen

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/CGvZN3N_L_c)

## Conspiracies

Made in the years I was in [Lou Reed’s band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/) and working with him on [*Lulu*](/conspiracies/lulu/). The electronics are the same work I did on stage, through [Kyma](/devices/).

The exchange: Gabriel’s *Scratch My Back*, 2010, covered twelve artists including Reed. Each was invited to cover Gabriel in return; the returns became *And I’ll Scratch Yours*, 2013.

The credit is mine. Discogs lists the track and its length.

Lou's approach to the song was amazing, super simple, guitar and voice with a minimal beat he programmed first. He brought me in help with the mix and the percussion crescendo at the end.

# “Peggy Sue”

“Peggy Sue” is [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/)’s recording of the Buddy Holly song for *Rave On Buddy Holly*, the tribute compilation released by Fantasy and Concord in June 2011, alongside Paul McCartney, Patti Smith, Florence and the Machine and the Black Keys. I play bass on it, a Moog Little Phatty. Three minutes nineteen.

![Cover of Rave On Buddy Holly.](/images/art-rave-on-buddy-holly.jpg)

Cover, *Rave On Buddy Holly*, 2011.

The credit: Discogs, [release 2948749](https://www.discogs.com/release/2948749), track 17: Lou Reed, “Peggy Sue.” Sarth Calhoun, bass, Little Phatty. On [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/rave-on-buddy-holly-bonus-track-version/1440953567).

## Listen

[Embedded player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/jvyzMkaY5xQ)

## What was written about it

Apple Music’s note on the album calls Reed’s take the sound of a cement mixer grinding the tune to a nub. Far Out remembers it as raw, punky. It sits at track seventeen of nineteen.

> Lou Reed tackles Buddy Holly’s classic hit ‘Peggy Sue’ the best way he knows how -- with distortion, fuzz and feedback.
> 
> [Ultimate Classic Rock](https://ultimateclassicrock.com/lou-reed-peggy-sue-song-review/), song review, 2011

The compilation: Nineteen acts on Buddy Holly songs, 2011. Fantasy Records with MPL. Reed’s is the only track Sarth plays on.

## Conspiracies

Recorded while I was in [Lou Reed’s band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/), which I joined in 2008. The bass here is a Moog synthesizer, not the electric upright [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/) played on stage.

Credit from Discogs. Label and line-up from the release and its press.

# The Creation of the Universe

https://www.sarth.net/transmissions/the-creation-of-the-universe/

[Transmissions](/transmissions/) / The Creation of the Universe

Transmission · Dream

# *The Creation of the Universe*

*The Creation of the Universe* is a double live album by Lou Reed’s Metal Machine Trio: [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/), [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/) and me. It was recorded over two nights at REDCAT in Los Angeles, October 2 and 3, 2008, the concerts that became [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/), and released in May 2009 on Reed’s Sister Ray Recordings under the Best Seat in the House banner.

Two tracks, *Night 1* and *Night 2*, each about fifty-five minutes.

![Cover of The Creation of the Universe by Lou Reed's Metal Machine Trio.](/images/art-creation-of-the-universe.jpg)

Cover, *The Creation of the Universe*, 2009.

> We have formed a recording unit called BEST SEAT IN THE HOUSE. We intend to put out different types of my music - from industrial to meditative to songs and all subway stops in between. CREATE!
> 
> Lou Reed, as quoted on Sarth’s site

## How it was recorded

We recorded the sets with a matched pair of Schoeps and a stereo Royer, and released them as they were -- pure ambient microphone tracks with no direct lines. That stuff was released as a double live CD, “Creation of the Universe.” This was the start of the group which was eventually renamed The Metal Machine Trio, and we went on to play in Europe, Brazil, and Australia.

We called the music “Deep Noise” because that’s what it was. At times though, it felt almost like improvised classical music, or something which didn’t have a name.

## Listen

[Embedded player](https://embed.music.apple.com/us/album/the-creation-of-the-universe/315196713)

The record: Night 1, fifty-five minutes. Night 2, fifty-six. On [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-creation-of-the-universe/315196713) and [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/1583151-Lou-Reed-s-Metal-Machine-Trio-The-Creation-Of-The-Universe).

> The REDCAT stage looked like a rehearsal room Friday night when Lou Reed, Ulrich Krieger and Sarth Calhoun took the stage.
> 
> Ann Powers, [Los Angeles Times, October 4, 2008](https://web.archive.org/web/20110312081628/http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/soundboard/2008/10/lou-reed-and-ul.html)

## The nights

The album is the two REDCAT nights billed as *Unclassified: Lou Reed and Ulrich Krieger*, the shows that sold out inside a day and had a late set added. [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lou-reed-oct-3-2008-los-angeles-redcatcalarts-theater-1043833/) heard me seated behind a desk with computers and mixers adding chunky layers of sub-frequency bass vibrations to the mix.

The later [ambisonic installation](/conspiracies/creation-of-the-universe-ambisonic/) of the same name uses a different recording, from the Gramercy show of April 24, 2009, not this album. The dates are on [Sightings](/sightings/).

## Conspiracies

Made by [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/), the trio’s first release. The processing ran through [Kyma](/devices/); the instrument was the Continuum. The press on the record and the shows is on [Rumors](/rumors/).

Who played what: Lou Reed, guitar, electronics and a small Continuum. Ulrich Krieger, tenor saxophone and live electronics. Sarth Calhoun, Continuum, and the whole field processed through Kyma.

My account and the Lou Reed line are from the Conspiracies page of my old Squarespace site. Release data from Apple Music and Discogs.

# *The Family Album*

*The Family Album* is the only full-length by [Lucibel Crater](/conspiracies/lucibel-crater/), the Brooklyn trio of [Leah Coloff](/conspirators/leah-coloff/), [Paul Chuffo](/conspirators/paul-chuffo/) and me. Ten songs, released February 12, 2008 on Searching Eye Records and mixed by [Bryce Goggin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Goggin).

[Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) plays guitar on “Threadbare Funeral.” It is the only guitar on the record.

![Cover of The Family Album by Lucibel Crater.](/images/art-the-family-album.jpg)

Cover, *The Family Album*, 2008.

The songs: 1. There Was a Time. 2. Your Mean Mouth. 3. Into the Bushes. 4. Threadbare Funeral, featuring Lou Reed. 5. Next of Kin. 6. Blue Stationwagon. 7. Where You Are. 8. Bones. 9. Swimmers. 10. Could_i.

## The songs

Ross Christopher at awaken music picked out “Where You Are,” “There was a Time” and “Threadbare Funeral.” MP3 Troll noted the Lou Reed guitar in May 2008, before the reviews. Coloff sings and plays cello; Chuffo plays drums; I play keys, bass, loops, [Kyma and the Continuum](/devices/).

Vogue Italia, January 2009: Ten muscular tracks and only one guitar, Lou Reed’s.

## Listen

The credit: *The Family Album*, Searching Eye Records, 2008, by Lucibel Crater: Leah Coloff, cello and voice; Paul Chuffo, drums; Sarth Calhoun, keys, bass, loops, Kyma and Continuum. Lou Reed, guitar, on “Threadbare Funeral.” Mixed by Bryce Goggin. On [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/album/5GWIntdZRNl8zc9rAsIrKD) and [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/album/the-family-album/274792742).

> I can’t begin to express how rare and nice it is to hear a band doing something angular and different! Lucibel Crater’s, The Family Album is just that - angular and clearly unique.
> 
> Ross Christopher, [awaken music, April 1, 2009](http://awakenmusic.blogspot.com/2009/04/family-album-lucibel-crater.html), five stars of five

## What was written about it

Simone Tempia wrote it up twice in Italy, in *Urban* in February 2009, where the Björk and White Stripes comparison comes from (Ci si può sentire qualcosa di Björk e magari dei White Stripes. Ma la verità è che il loro sound è unico e difficilmente incasellabile.), and in *Vogue Italia* that January. [Lost in Sound](http://lostinsound.org/lucibel-crater-not-your-dads-jazz/) interviewed the band in February 2010. The rest is on [Rumors](/rumors/).

The band’s earlier EP is [*Miracles*](/transmissions/miracles/), 2007. My tools on it are on [Devices](/devices/).

Lucibel Crater: Leah Coloff, Sarth Calhoun, Paul Chuffo.

The record was paid for out of [mp3.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mp3.com) downloads. # Introspections

https://www.sarth.net/transmissions/introspections/

[Transmissions](/transmissions/) / Introspections

Transmission · Dream

# Introspections

*Introspections* is a series of improvised drone pieces I recorded and filmed from 2015, on Continuum and Kyma, with duet partners. Three are public: “For Lovers,” with [Jacob McCoy](/conspirators/jacob-mccoy/), filmed on March 2, 2015; “Sunset Meditation,” on SoundCloud; and a clip from the Warper Party in New York, September 2015.

Musical explorations that build on the Tai Chi and Meditation tracks I did with Lou Reed, and the shows we did with Ulrich Krieger as The Metal Machine Trio. Drones, improvised transformation, and hypnotic symbols create a collaborative sound field. I’ve explored these ideas in venues ranging from Lolapalooza, The Royal Festival Hall in London, and The Sydney Opera house ... to some of my favorite performances at intimate events.

![Sarth Calhoun bent over a Continuum Fingerboard, black and white.](/images/sarth-top-know-square.jpg)

Sarth Calhoun at the Continuum.

For Lovers: On March 2nd, 2015, Jacob and I got together to record some Linnstrument / Continuum Fingerboard duets. It was also Lou Reed’s birthday, and this piece reminded me of things we explored together. Drones, close intervals, sum and difference frequencies. And Lou loved his Continuum Fingerboard. So this is dedicated to him.

## For Lovers

Eight minutes thirteen, with Jacob McCoy on Linnstrument. Released as a [single](/transmissions/singles/) in 2020. On [Vimeo](https://vimeo.com/125323250).

[Embedded player](https://player.vimeo.com/video/125323250)

## Sunset Meditation

A solo piece, on SoundCloud under the name noisegroove.

[Embedded player](https://w.soundcloud.com/player/?url=https%3A//api.soundcloud.com/tracks/201344917&color=%23111111&auto_play=false&show_artwork=true)

> Imagine stillness moving through space. If Energy flows where attention goes, where does it take you? What shall we make of it? Who Are You? Who Am I? What really Matters?
> 
> Sarth Calhoun, the Introspections page of his own site

[Embedded player](https://player.vimeo.com/video/140015309)

## Warper Party, 2015

Forty-one seconds from a Warper Party set in New York, September 2015. On [Vimeo](https://vimeo.com/140015309).

## Reflections

I have been fortunate enough to explore these ideas with great improvisers, including [Laurie Anderson](/conspirators/laurie-anderson/), [Moldover](/conspirators/moldover/), [John Zorn](/conspirators/john-zorn/), [Sxip Shirey](/conspirators/sxip-shirey/), [Marc Ribot](/conspirators/marc-ribot/) and [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/). In the first video, Sxip is creating the drones and structure using an amplified shruti box, while I play continuum. In the second, Jacob McCoy creates drones on the Linnstrument. I worked with sound artist Michael Clemow on a project called “The Drost Effect” ... named for the phenomenon known also as mise en abyme, two mirrors face each other and create endless reflections ... in our process we each sampled and transformed the other’s sound creating realtime infinite recursion.

[Shruti box, with Sxip Shirey](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_ZinrLAl4I) · [Prepared guitar, with Sxip Shirey](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8jgV_4Xqmc) · [Linnstrument, with Jacob McCoy](https://vimeo.com/125323250)

## Contemplations

What is the dialogue between sound and consciousness? I worked with Jeremiah Brimlau to bring this work to retreat centers and yoga studios. His guided meditations helped the audience to move through the sound experience.

## Conspiracies

It builds on the meditation music I made with [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) and on [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) with [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/). The instruments are on [Devices](/devices/).

The credit: Introspections: Sarth Calhoun, Continuum Fingerboard and Kyma, improvised drone duets from 2015 with Jacob McCoy, Linnstrument; Sxip Shirey, shruti box and prepared guitar; and others.

My paragraphs are from the Introspections pages of my old Squarespace site, put in the past tense, and my Vimeo note for For Lovers.

# Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009

# *Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009*

*Lou Reed Live at Lollapalooza 2009* is the official DVD of [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/)’s set at Lollapalooza in Grant Park, Chicago, on Sunday, August 9, 2009, released July 19, 2011. The band was Mike Rathke and Steve Hunter on guitars, Kevin Hearn on keyboards, [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/) on bass, Tony “Thunder” Smith on drums, [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/) on saxophone, and me on electronics and Continuum.

![Sarth Calhoun performing at Lollapalooza, a bass headstock in the foreground.](/images/lolla-dvd-show.jpg)

Sarth Calhoun at Lollapalooza, August 9, 2009.

> Reed, on the other hand, brought the weekend’s most audacious music, a set laced with bile, violence and feedback, never more so than when he threaded a raging “Paranoia Key of E” into a pile-driving “Waiting for the Man.”
> 
> Greg Kot, [Chicago Tribune, August 10, 2009](https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/08/10/lollapalooza-does-it-again/)

## The set

Day three, to a capacity crowd of forty thousand. [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lou-reed-snarls-vampire-weekend-bounce-on-eclectic-lollapalooza-day-three-2-65494/) noted Reed ran fifteen minutes over. Inside the set, [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) played a ten minute noise interlude between the songs. The date is on [Sightings](/sightings/).

## The interlude

Ulrich Krieger, writing after Reed died: At 2009’s Lollapalooza MM3 played a ten minute noise interlude between well known Reed songs to the frantic cheers of a large audience. And of the tours that followed: On subsequent tours with his newly revised rock group, including Sarth and me, he would play MM3 recordings before and after shows.

Credits: From [loureed.com](https://loureed.com/news/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009-dvd/): Mike Rathke, guitar. Steve Hunter, guitar. Kevin Hearn, keyboards. Rob Wasserman, bass. Tony “Thunder” Smith, drums. Ulrich Krieger, saxophone. Sarth Calhoun, electronics and continuum. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/15272070) lists it on Sister Ray Enterprises, Sarth credited for Continuum fingerboard and processing.

> Rob Wasserman’s upright electric bass, Kevin Hearn’s string/horn patches, Sarth Calhoun’s invisible Macbookery, and guitarist Steve Hunter’s fiery if decidedly inside-the-box solos.
> 
> Jesse Jarnow on the same band a year earlier, [The Village Voice, May 6, 2008](https://villagevoice.com/2008/05/06/live-lou-reed-at-the-highline-ballrooms-first-birthday-party)

## Conspiracies

This is [Lou Reed’s song band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-song-band/) on film, with [Metal Machine Trio](/conspiracies/metal-machine-trio/) inside it. [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/) and [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/) have their own pages. My rig that day was the Continuum and [Kyma](/devices/).

Credits verbatim from loureed.com. The Krieger lines are from “Unclassifiable,” [The Wire](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/lou-reed-1942-2013_ulrich-krieger_unclassifiable), 2013.

# About Awakening (To Blacklist)

https://www.sarth.net/transmissions/about-awakening-to-blacklist/

Nov 21, 2020 · Message

# About Awakening (To Blacklist)

One of my favorite things about this track is the morph from the hum to a rhythmic/pitched pattern.

There’s a scene in ‘Book of Sarth’ where the office workers are coming out of a daze, they are transitioning back in to reality, and the hum transforming really ended up matching this perfectly. (I don’t know which idea came first.)

Here’s how I did it:

I start with a recording of typical 60 cycle hum. This was pretty straightforward, I probably just messed with a 1/4” cable partially plugged into my Marshall amp, or something similar.

[Listen](/audio/hum-plain.m4a)

Plain 60 cycle hum.

I wanted to see if I could transform that sound into something.

I started playback and threw various Ableton plug-ins on the track.

![Ableton device chain: Delay, EQ Eight, Compressor, Frequency Shifter.](/images/awakening-chain.png)

The chain in Ableton: Delay, EQ Eight, Compressor, Frequency Shifter.

I tried a Delay, an EQ, a compressor … and they all stayed, but what made the melody was the frequency shifter plug-in. I saw a preset called ‘Space Birds’ and with it on the track, I immediately got a cool melody.

[Listen](/audio/hum-melody.m4a)

The hum melody.

![Ableton Frequency Shifter on the Spacebirds preset.](/images/awakening-spacebirds.png)

The Frequency Shifter on the Spacebirds preset.

It’s a pitch shifter with a random waveform modulating the pitch.

It’s moving at a speed of one quarter note, or so it says, but I hear it as sixteenths (the file is at 88.00 BPM so …) I think maybe that has to do with the width control.

Then it’s just a matter of automating the wet/dry control to ‘morph’ the track from plain hum to the melody.

![An automation curve in Ableton rising and falling across the clip.](/images/awakening-automation.png)

The wet/dry automation, from hum to melody.

One of the great things about Ableton is the plugins, no matter what type, usually have some kind of wet/dry or ‘percent’ control. This allow for a lot of cool morphs and transitions, I’ll go deeper down that road in the next post.

---

The other thing I love about this track is the drum sounds during this hum/intro section. There is the extremely clear track and a more … gnarly track. Here they are combined, but I put a bit of strong panning so you can more easily differentiate the two parts

[Listen](/audio/hum-drums-combined.m4a)

Both drum tracks, panned apart.

Here’s just the 606 (clear) loop:

[Listen](/audio/hum-606-loop.m4a)

The 606 loop.

And here is the sampled club kit with brushes:

[Listen](/audio/hum-club-kit-brushes.m4a)

The sampled club kit with brushes.

And then the dramatic, almost military hits that come in and out have the gnarliness much more evident.

[Listen](/audio/hum-military-hits.m4a)

The military hits.

This was a happy accident. The original piece (called Onamanopeia April Foolz) was an instrumental done at 176.10 BPM. At the time I was having issues with cpu power in that particular file, so I ‘froze’ a couple of the drum tracks.

For whatever reason, when I started working on the hum piece, I halved the BPM to 88, and I forgot to unfreeze those two tracks.

This meant that the beats played at the much slower tempo, but one track was just slowed via midi, maintaining the very clear pristine quality, and the other was audio-stretched, making it very gnarly. This was particularly awesome because it was an exaggeration of what I was going for. I often have two (or more) drum kits on a track, one pristine, one dirty. This was just more so.

If you want to hear the entire track on Spotify, including it’s connection to the vocal track ‘Blacklist’ here it is:

[Embedded player](https://open.spotify.com/embed/album/2AK3ADNcGHccdecSkjV43k)

More about happy accidents and automated effect controls to morph sources in future posts. I hope you enjoy!

— Sarth

Posted on sarth.net on November 21, 2020, and reproduced here as written, with the audio examples and screenshots from that post. The track is [“Awakening (To Blacklist)”](/conspiracies/awakening-to-blacklist/), from [*The Book of Sarth*](/conspiracies/book-of-sarth/).

---

# Sightings

# Sightings

A record of shows and installations. *The Creation of the Universe* comes from two nights at REDCAT, October 2–3, 2008. The later ambisonic installation uses a different recording, made at the Gramercy show on April 24, 2009.

## Spine

1. **Metal Machine Trio (Unclassified) at REDCAT, Los Angeles · Oct 2–3, 2008.** World premiere billed as *Unclassified: [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) and [Ulrich Krieger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulrich_Krieger)*. Three performances: Thu 2 Oct 8:30pm, added late show Thu 2 Oct 10:30pm, Fri 3 Oct 8:30pm. Me on Continuum and live processing. Official live album *The Creation of the Universe* is the unedited recording of those two nights.
2. **Metal Machine Trio, Blender Theater at Gramercy, New York · Apr 23–24, 2009.** First NYC stand. [John Zorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Zorn) sat in on the 24th. This night’s recording later became the CSULB / Cranbrook ambisonic installation.
3. **Yellow Pony with Lou Reed and [Laurie Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Anderson) · Europe, Jul and Aug–Sep 2009.** Eight-city tour billed *The Yellow Pony and Other Songs and Stories*. Me on Continuum and live voice re-sampling, center stage. Two short tours.
4. **Lou Reed at Lollapalooza, Grant Park, Chicago · Aug 9, 2009.** Day three. Metal Machine Trio played a ten minute noise interlude inside Reed’s set. Me on Continuum and live processing.
5. **Metal Machine Trio Europe · “A Night of Deep Noise,” Apr 17–30, 2010.** Nine dates, UK through Palma de Mallorca.
6. **Metal Machine Trio, [Sydney Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House) (Opera Theatre) · May 30, 2010.** [Vivid LIVE](/conspiracies/vivid-live/). Anderson’s *Transitory Life* was a separate Drama Theatre program, June 1 and 2.
7. **Metal Machine Trio, Sesc Pinheiros, São Paulo · Nov 20–21, 2010.** Two nights.
8. **Ambisonic installation *The Creation of the Universe*** · CSULB University Art Museum, Long Beach, 27 Jan–Apr 15, 2012; restaged [Cranbrook Art Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranbrook_Art_Museum), Bloomfield Hills, Nov 21, 2015–Mar 26, 2016. Playback of the Gramercy 2009 recording.

The two nights in São Paulo were the last Metal Machine Trio concerts.

## Metal Machine Trio

Billing: Lou Reed, guitar, electronics, Continuum. Ulrich Krieger, tenor sax, live electronics. Sarth Calhoun, Continuum, live processing through Kyma. Flyers: “No songs. No vocals.” and “A Night of Deep Noise.”

- **October 2, 2008** · REDCAT / CalArts Theater, Walt Disney Concert Hall complex, Los Angeles. Unclassified: Lou Reed and Ulrich Krieger. World premiere. 8:30pm and added late show 10:30pm.

  [REDCAT archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20110927041818/http://www.redcat.org/event/lou-reed-and-ulrich-krieger) · recording: album Night 1

- **October 3, 2008** · REDCAT, Los Angeles. 8:30pm.

  [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lou-reed-oct-3-2008-los-angeles-redcatcalarts-theater-1043833/) · recording: album Night 2

- **April 23, 2009** · Blender Theater at Gramercy, New York. A Night of Deep Noise. 8:30pm.

  [NYT Ratliff](https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/25/arts/music/25reed.html) · [Village Voice](https://www.villagevoice.com/lou-reeds-metal-machine-trio/)

- **April 24, 2009** · Blender Theater at Gramercy, New York. Special guest John Zorn. Source tape for the CSULB/Cranbrook installation. Not commercially issued.

  [Variety](https://variety.com/2009/music/markets-festivals/lou-reed-3-1117940137/)

- **August 9, 2009** · Lollapalooza, Grant Park, Chicago. Day three, to a capacity crowd of 40,000. A Metal Machine Trio section inside Lou Reed’s set.

  Reed’s own site called it “a particular highlight”: his ‘Metal Machine Trio’ section featuring Ulrich Krieger and Sarth Calhoun.

  [Announcement](https://loureed.com/news/lou-reed-at-lollapalooza/) · [DVD credits](https://loureed.com/news/lou-reed-live-at-lollapalooza-2009-dvd/) · [Ulrich Krieger, The Wire](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/lou-reed-1942-2013_ulrich-krieger_unclassifiable) · [Chicago Tribune](https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/08/10/lollapalooza-does-it-again/)

- **April 17, 2010** · The Junction, Cambridge, UK. Start of nine-date Europe tour.

- **April 18, 2010** · O2 Academy, Oxford, UK.

- **April 19, 2010** · Royal Festival Hall, London, UK (Ether Festival).

- **April 21, 2010** · La Cigale, Paris, France. Announced widely.

- **April 22, 2010** · Ancienne Belgique, Brussels, Belgium (Domino Festival).

- **April 24, 2010** · DR Koncerthuset, Copenhagen, Denmark.

- **April 26, 2010** · Oslo, Norway. Announced as Sentrum Scene; eyewitness blogs say Rockefeller, a sister room in the same complex.

- **April 27, 2010** · Ole Bull Scene, Bergen, Norway (Bergenfest).

- **April 30, 2010** · Teatre Principal, Palma de Mallorca, Spain (Festival Alternatilla).

- **May 30, 2010** · Opera Theatre, Sydney Opera House. [Vivid LIVE](/conspiracies/vivid-live/).

- **November 20, 2010** and **November 21, 2010** · Teatro Paulo Autran, Sesc Pinheiros, São Paulo.

## Installations · not concerts

- **January 27, 2012 – April 15, 2012** · University Art Museum, CSULB, Long Beach. Ambisonic playback of Gramercy 2009 night 2 (Zorn). Visitors stand in Lou’s, Ulrich’s, or my position on stage.

- **November 21, 2015 – March 26, 2016** · Cranbrook Art Museum, Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. Restaging. 12 loudspeakers. After Reed’s death; playback only.

  [Cranbrook](https://cranbrookartmuseum.org/exhibition/lou-reed-metal-machine-trio-the-creation-of-the-universe/)

## Yellow Pony · Lou Reed and Laurie Anderson

Continuum fingerboard and live resampling of their voices. Center of the stage, like a drummer.

- **July 10, 2009** · Festival de la Porta Ferrada, Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Spain. Present at the press conference.
- **July 12, 2009** · Plaza del Obradoiro, Santiago de Compostela, Spain.
- **July 14, 2009** · Los Veranos de la Villa, Madrid, Spain.
- **July 16, 2009** · DR Koncerthuset, Copenhagen, Denmark. Named onstage.
- **July 18, 2009** · Palace Theatre, Manchester, UK. “electronic sound manipulator… between them” ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/jul/20/laurie-anderson-lou-reed-review)).
- **August 30, 2009** · Huvilateltta, Helsinki, Finland.
- **September 2, 2009** · Jahrhunderthalle, Frankfurt, Germany. Electronics, named in program and reviews.
- **September 4, 2009** · Salle Pleyel, Paris. Billed “claviers et électronique.”

## Lucibel Crater

Line-up: Sarth Calhoun, keys, bass, loops, Kyma, Continuum. Leah Coloff, cello and voice. Paul Chuffo, drums.

- **February 27, 2007** · Knitting Factory main space, NYC, with Subtle.
- **March 8, 2007** · FatBaby, 112 Rivington St, NYC.
- **April 3, 2007** · The Delancey, NYC (WARPER).
- **November 23, 2008** · RAW-Tempel, Berlin. Lucibel Crater N.Y. Video *Holy, Then, Now · Berlin Live* shot here.
- **March 4, 2009** · The Delancey, NYC (WARPER). Downstairs 8:20, a solo slot for me on the printed bill.

## Lou Reed song band, 2011

The [eight-piece band](/conspiracies/lou-reed-2011-european-tour/): me on Continuum with multiple Kyma/Paca systems, [Kevin Hearn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hearn), [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/), Tony Smith, [Rob Wasserman](/conspirators/rob-wasserman/), Aram Bajakian and [Tony Diodore](/conspirators/tony-diodore/).

- July 2, 2011 Hop Farm, Paddock Wood · 07-04 Hammersmith Apollo, London · 07-05 Le Grand Rex, Paris · 07-08 Arena Civica, Milan (on some lists) · 07-10 Piazza Duomo, Pistoia · 07-16 Italia Wave, Lecce · 07-17 Les Vieilles Charrues, Carhaix · 07-18 Greek Theatre, Taormina · 07-22 Nuovo Festival Del Vittoriale, Gardone Riviera · 07-23 Piazza Matteotti, Sogliano al Rubicone · 07-25 Parco della Musica Cavea, Rome · 07-26 Les Nuits de Fourvière, Lyon.

## Lulu

Electronics on *[Lulu](/conspiracies/lulu/)*, 2011, and Continuum drones on the tapes made before [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica), as David Fricke described them. I directed rehearsals of the score for Robert Wilson’s Berlin *Lulu*. [Junior Dad](/conspiracies/junior-dad/) began at Lou’s apartment with Rob Wasserman and Kyma.

- **November 2011** · The first live performances of the *Lulu* material, with Lou Reed and Metallica: *Later... with Jools Holland* in London, *Taratata* in Paris, and five songs in Cologne. Got to play some of these Lulu tracks on the Jools Holland show … the first live performances of this material! and Had a great time performing 5 songs from Lulu in Cologne … it was such an intense experience. From my posts of November 9 and 12, 2011.

## Later

- **April 9, 2014** · SOHO Gallery for Digital Arts, New York. Gralbum / Book of Sarth app launch. Exhibition, not a concert.

  [Stereophile](https://www.stereophile.com/content/gralbum-re-thinking-concept-album)

- **April 1, 2015** · New York Transit Museum, Brooklyn. Launch showing of the *Train O’ Thots* gralbum, Tom Hart with Moon Hooch, from [The Gralbum Collective](/conspiracies/gralbum-collective/). An event, not a concert.

- **March 13, 2019** · Cathedral of St. John the Divine, New York. Lou Reed Drones for Reed’s 77th birthday. Continuum / electronics, with Laurie Anderson, John Zorn, Stewart Hurwood, Stan Harrison, Shahzad Ismaily.

- **August 3, 2019** · Prospect Park Bandshell, Brooklyn. International Lou Reed Tai Chi Day / BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn! With Laurie Anderson, John Zorn and Stewart Hurwood.

- **March 2, 2023** · Brookfield Place Winter Garden. Lou Reed’s 81st birthday. Guest performance with Kevin Hearn, Shahzad Ismaily, Laurie Anderson, against Lou Reed’s Musical Drones (Stewart Hurwood).

## One-offs

  Reed’s own site: Reed performed an amazing set including ‘Dirty Blvd.’ and ‘Who Am I’ with Mike Rathke on guitar and Sarth Calhoun on electronic processing.

# Rumors

Press on the work, quoted exactly as published. I made Metal Machine Trio with [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) and [Ulrich Krieger](/conspirators/ulrich-krieger/), and wrote the original *Lulu* score with Reed for [Robert Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Wilson_(director)); the [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica) album grew from those recordings.

## Book of Sarth

- > Things really come alive in what’s called the ‘director’s view’: tap an image and the artwork fills the screen, putting the reader in the same place as the characters.

  > Calhoun’s music is no doubt experimental, but his tracks and the artwork play nimbly off one another.

  [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2013/1/3/3828314/the-book-of-sarth-ipad-app-graphic-novel-concept-album) · Bryan Bishop · Jan 3, 2013

- > The app format seems like a completely new medium to work in. Music always needs a new medium, because it’s always changing. I think if music doesn’t have technology on its side, it tends to have the problem of where to go, it starts to run out of steam.

  Sarth Calhoun, [Tumblr Storyboard](https://web.archive.org/web/20140812122953/http://storyboard.tumblr.com/post/41358319321/the-book-of-sarth-an-interactive-cyberpunk-tale) · ~Jan 24, 2013

  [The Eighth Nerve](https://news.symbolicsound.com/2012/11/the-book-of-sarth/) · Nov 2012

- > I wouldn’t mind rolling a j before playing with this trippy app.

## Metal Machine Trio

- > The duo took the stage along with Sarth Calhoun, a computer-based sound designer… Calhoun, seated behind a desk with computers and mixers, added chunky layers of sub-frequency bass vibrations to the mix.

  [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lou-reed-oct-3-2008-los-angeles-redcatcalarts-theater-1043833/) · Jeffrey Overwood · Oct 8, 2008 · REDCAT

- > On Thursday night at the Blender Theater at Gramercy, onstage between Sarth Calhoun and Ulrich Krieger, two much younger musicians, he was making noise — improvised, loud, heavily processed, and some of it ugly enough to make people leave.

  [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/25/arts/music/25reed.html) · Ben Ratliff · Apr 25, 2009

- > teaming with the composer and saxophonist Ulrich Krieger and the multi-instrumentalist Sarth Calhoun to create ‘a night of deep noise.’

  [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/17/arts/music/17pop.html) · listing · Apr 17, 2009

- > It would be too warm and fuzzy to suggest that he engaged bandmate Sarth Calhoun — who did much of his work on a laptop — in any sort of interplay, but the two did combine to create a formidable wall of sound.

  [Variety](https://variety.com/2009/music/markets-festivals/lou-reed-3-1117940137/) · David Sprague · Apr 27, 2009

- > Calhoun started playing his Continuum as if it was a throbbing Hammond organ, creating a low undulating swarm of sound.

  [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lou-reed-brings-controversial-metal-machine-music-to-life-114478/) · Apr 2009

- > Lou decided to bring Sarth along at the last minute; he met him at tai chi practice, played with him at home and wanted his electronic sounds for this concert.

  Ulrich Krieger, [The Wire](https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/essays/lou-reed-1942-2013_ulrich-krieger_unclassifiable) · 2013 · “Unclassifiable”

- > Lou said, I don’t want to play duo, I have this electronic guy in New York and I’d like to bring him along. So he brought Sarth Calhoun in.

  Ulrich Krieger, [OC Weekly](https://www.ocweekly.com/metal-machine-trios-ulrich-krieger-the-trio-is-an-update-of-lou-reeds-metal-machine-music-in-philosophical-and-aesthetic-sense-6581450/) · Jan 27, 2012

- [SPIN](https://www.spinmagazine.com/2009/04/lou-reed-unleashes-metal-machine-music-nyc/) · John Macdonald · Apr 24, 2009 · names the Continuum Fingerboard

# Devices

https://www.sarth.net/devices/

Physical objects · Machine

# Devices

Physical objects on the table. Kyma, Continuum, the performance DAW, the motion studio. Software machines are on [Contraptions](/contraptions/).

## Symbolic Sound Kyma (Paca / Pacarana)

A graphical sound-design environment. The Paca is dedicated DSP hardware, a small orange box, rack-mountable, not a plugin inside a laptop. Maker: Symbolic Sound Corporation (Carla Scaletti and Kurt Hebel), Champaign, Illinois. [kyma.symbolicsound.com](https://kyma.symbolicsound.com/)

I beta-tested Kyma and am credited on the Kyma X startup screen. Lucibel Crater looping and processing. Metal Machine Trio: live Kyma processing of the band. 2011 [Lou Reed](/conspirators/lou-reed/) European tour: multiple rack-mounted Pacas. *Lulu* at the [Berliner Ensemble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berliner_Ensemble): Kyma processing and Continuum/Kyma playing. The Book of Sarth score is Kyma-drenched. I built SeqOSC in it, a new kind of synthesis, a relative of AM synthesis derived from exploring the analogies between rhythm and timbre. Junior Dad: Wasserman’s electric upright through Kyma, first session at Lou’s apartment.

[Euro tour](https://news.symbolicsound.com/2011/07/lou-reeds-euro-tour/) · [Book of Sarth](https://news.symbolicsound.com/2012/11/the-book-of-sarth/)

## Haken Continuum Fingerboard

A long neoprene playing surface that tracks finger position and pressure in three dimensions. Continuous pitch, not keys. Often driving Kyma. Maker: Lippold Haken / Haken Audio, Champaign, Illinois. [hakenaudio.com](https://www.hakenaudio.com/)

Lucibel Crater and the Reed years. In Metal Machine Trio, Lou and I both had Continuums onstage. Yellow Pony: Continuum plus live resampling of Reed and Anderson’s voices. *Lulu*: dual Continuum improvisations with a live string section. Wikipedia names me as an advocate.

After watching videos of me playing it at Lollapalooza, Lippold Haken said: I lost sleep. I even dreamt about it last night. It was one of those thousands-of-people-watching nightmares.

[Continuum Fingerboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuum_Fingerboard) · [Walking the road that only you can see](https://news.symbolicsound.com/2012/10/walking-the-road-that-only-you-can-see/)

## Ableton Live

A DAW that treats clips, warping, and devices as a performance instrument. Maker: Ableton AG, Berlin. [ableton.com](https://www.ableton.com/en/live/)

I was an [Ableton Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ableton_Live) endorser; the 2008 REDCAT program and the 2014 Asia Society *Sunken Cathedral* notes say so. The Book of Sarth track “Awakening (To Blacklist)” was built in Live: 60 cycle hum run through plugins until a frequency shifter became the melody. [How I did it](/transmissions/about-awakening-to-blacklist/), with the audio.

## Runway

Generative video and image studio. The motion end of Visual Reference Prompting. Maker: Runway AI, Inc. [runwayml.com](https://runwayml.com/)

Burlap connects to Runway. I entered Runway’s 48-hour film competition in the spring of 2025, and [Burlap](/conspiracies/burlap/) came out of that: the toolchain was just unworkable, just completely unworked for anything I wanted to do or how I thought a professional workspace should be.

## Bass

My first instrument. In my teens I stopped buying comic books to save up for my first bass guitar. Number19: bass and keys. Lucibel Crater: keys, bass, loops. Reed’s [“Peggy Sue”](/transmissions/peggy-sue/) (*Rave On Buddy Holly*): bass, a Moog Little Phatty.

# Citations

Every outbound link on this site, grouped by the page it appears on. Machine readable: [citations.json](/citations.json).

## What first-party means here

This site is a primary source. Sarth Calhoun is the author, the publisher and the subject, so there is no gap between the source and the person describing it. Wikipedia and Wikidata require independent reliable sources because they are written by strangers who cannot verify him. That standard belongs to those projects.

Links are here so a reader or an agent can follow a claim to further evidence, and so entities resolve unambiguously. Where a claim carries no link, no public source has been found for it. That is not a measure of how reliable it is.

Resolve the person through [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarth_Calhoun), [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7424654), [MusicBrainz](https://musicbrainz.org/artist/e6ac65c7-146f-44bc-9acd-002633185c4f), [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/artist/2310400-Sarth-Calhoun) or [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/6uUtOazhiVXfNU8KAglFv9). The full set is in the JSON-LD `sameAs` on every page.

# Search

## Reading it another way

Everything the search box uses is a file you can fetch. [pages.json](/pages.json) is the catalogue: every page with its title, description, facet, date and headings, and a link to its markdown. [search-index.json](/search-index.json) is the index behind this box, scored so that a page about a thing outranks a page that merely mentions it.

Every page has a markdown twin beside it, at its own address with `index.md` on the end. [llms.txt](/llms.txt) is the short version of the whole site and [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) is all of it inlined. [citations.json](/citations.json) lists every outbound link, page by page. There is a [sitemap](/sitemap.xml) and a [feed](/feed.xml).
